43046605.title: Genomic ascertainment of PALB2-related cancer predisposition.
43046605.author: Stewart DR
43046605.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer risk arising from a germline pathogenic PALB2 variant ascertained through a personal or family history of cancer has been well-studied. Here, we used genomic ascertainment to quantify PALB2-associated cancer risk, age-specific penetrance, all-cause and cancer-specific mortality.
METHODS: We conducted a case-control study in two large population-based adult cohorts: the UK Biobank (n = 469,580) and Geisinger MyCode (n = 167,050). PALB2 P/LP heterozygotes were identified via exome sequencing and compared with non-carriers. Cancer diagnoses and vital status were obtained from linked registry and electronic health record data. We used multivariable logistic regression to estimate odds ratios for cancer outcomes and Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios for all-cause mortality. Age-specific cumulative incidence (penetrance) was estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods. Models were adjusted for birth year, sex (when applicable), smoking status, and body mass index.
RESULTS: PALB2 P/LP variant prevalence was 1:571 in UK Biobank and 1:940 in MyCode, with the higher prevalence in the UK cohort driven by the PALB2 p.Trp1038Ter founder variant. Compared with non-carriers, heterozygotes had significantly increased odds of any cancer, female breast cancer and pancreatic cancer, in both cohorts (P < 0.01). Adjusted hazard ratios for any cancer and female breast cancer ranged from 1.7 to 3.6. All-cause mortality was increased among PALB2-heterozygotes (HR 1.61-1.67), and survival after cancer diagnosis was reduced. Family history further modified cancer risk.
CONCLUSIONS: Genomic ascertainment of PALB2-heterozygotes identifies elevated risk for multiple cancers and increased all-cause and cancer-specific mortality, although risks were lower than estimates from familial ascertainment.

43068558.title: The APA score stratifies prognosis in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma treated with atezolizumab-bevacizumab.
43068558.author: Campani C
43068558.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Atezolizumab-bevacizumab (AtezoBev) is one of the standard first-line therapy for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet clinical outcomes remain heterogeneous and robust prognostic tools are limited. We aimed to develop and externally validate the APA score, a simple prognostic model integrating tumour burden (AFP), tumour aggressiveness (PIVKA-II) and liver functional reserve (mALBI grade).
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 345 patients from two cohorts: a European derivation cohort (n = 129) and an Asian validation cohort (n = 216). Patients were classified into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk APA groups. Outcomes were overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and radiological response.
RESULTS: In the derivation cohort (median age 68; 85% male; 83% cirrhosis), elevated AFP and PIVKA-II were associated with adverse tumour features, including tumour size > 7 cm, macrovascular invasion, and infiltrative pattern (all p < 0.01). The APA score stratified patients into low-, intermediate- and high-risk groups with markedly different OS (not reached vs. 25.6 vs. 12.4 months; p < 0.001) and PFS (10.7 vs. 8.6 vs. 4.7 months; p = 0.004). In addition, the APA score demonstrated the highest prognostic performance among the tested models, outperforming BCLC, Child-Pugh, ALBI, CRAFITY, TBCS and CRAPT-M (bootstrap-corrected C-index: 0.66). These findings were confirmed in the independent Asian validation cohort. In exploratory analyses, early reductions in AFP and/or PIVKA-II before cycle 2 were associated with improved response, longer survival and tumour downstaging. Among biomarker-positive patients, 18.6% achieved an early dual biomarker decrease and were more frequently eligible for downstaging strategies (16-23%).
CONCLUSION: The APA score is a simple and clinically applicable tool that improves prognostic assessment in AtezoBev-treated HCC across populations with different etiologies and may support clinical risk stratification.

43063963.title: Organ-preserving multimodal therapy for patients with high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma in China (DISTINCT-I): a single-arm, phase 2 trial.
43063963.author: Huang J
43063963.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radical nephroureterectomy is the standard treatment for patients with high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma, but causes irreversible nephron loss and can limit subsequent systemic therapy. We aimed to assess a response-adapted kidney-preserving strategy integrating induction disitamab vedotin plus tislelizumab, selective kidney-sparing surgery, and longitudinal circulating tumour DNA and urinary tumour DNA monitoring in patients with localised high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma.
METHODS: DISTINCT-I was a single-arm, phase 2 trial conducted at two tertiary referral centres in China. Adults aged 18 years or older with histologically confirmed, localised, high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma (cT1-T3, N0-N1, M0), and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-2 received 2·0 mg/kg intravenous disitamab vedotin plus intravenous 200 mg tislelizumab once every 3 weeks for two to four cycles, followed by response-adapted kidney-sparing surgery when feasible. The primary endpoint was the 1-year kidney-intact event-free survival rate, assessed in the intention-to-treat population. Kidney-intact event-free survival was defined as the time from enrolment to the earliest occurrence of high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma recurrence, death from any cause, or conversion to radical nephroureterectomy. Safety was assessed in all patients who received at least one dose of study treatment and according to Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events and Clavien-Dindo classification. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05912816), and is ongoing.
FINDINGS: Between Sept 6, 2023, and Nov 15, 2024, 36 patients were assessed for eligibility; ten did not meet the eligibility criteria and six declined to participate. Of the 20 patients enrolled, 17 (85%) were male and three (15%) were female; all patients were Chinese. At data cutoff (Dec 31, 2025), median follow-up was 17·0 months (IQR 14·0-23·0). The 1-year kidney-intact event-free survival rate was 70% (95% CI 46-88; 14 participants). Grade 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in two (10%) patients (fatigue in one and increased γ-glutamyl transferase in another). No grade 4-5 treatment-related adverse events, serious treatment-related adverse events, or treatment-related deaths occurred.
INTERPRETATION: This structured, multimodal, response-adapted strategy was associated with kidney preservation in selected patients with high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma. These findings support further prospective comparative evaluation of organ-preserving strategies in patients with high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma.
FUNDING: Shanghai Science and Technology Commission, Shanghai Health Commission, Beijing Xisike Clinical Oncology Research Foundation, and Department of Science and Technology of Guangdong.
TRANSLATION: For the Chinese (Mandarin) translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

43063962.title: Prostate and pelvic nodal stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) versus prostate-only SBRT for high-risk, localised prostate cancer (PACE-NODES): early adverse event results from an international, open-label, phase 3, randomised controlled trial.
43063962.author: Pathmanathan A
43063962.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radiotherapy to the prostate and pelvic lymph nodes compared with prostate-only radiotherapy has shown benefits for high-risk prostate cancer in some studies, but evidence remains unclear. In low-risk or intermediate-risk disease, prostate-only stereotactic body radiotherapy (P-SBRT) is safe and effective. PACE-NODES aims to demonstrate safety and efficacy of prostate and pelvic nodal SBRT (PPN-SBRT) for high-risk disease.
METHODS: PACE-NODES is a phase 3, open-label, randomised trial conducted at 47 hospitals in the UK, Ireland, and New Zealand. The trial recruited men aged 18 years or older, with a WHO performance status of 0-2, and with high-risk (Gleason score 8-10, stage T3a-T4, or prostate-specific antigen >20 ng/mL), localised prostate adenocarcinoma, planned for at least 12 months of hormone therapy. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1), using minimisation with a random element, to P-SBRT (36·25 Gy prostate) or PPN-SBRT (36·25 Gy prostate, 25 Gy pelvic nodes) in five fractions, on alternate days. Neither participants nor researchers were masked to treatment allocation. The primary endpoint is time to biochemical or clinical failure (not yet mature). This preplanned safety analysis is on secondary endpoints, with a focus on Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events grade 2 or worse gastrointestinal and genitourinary adverse events within 12 weeks of treatment, analysed by treatment received. Patient-reported outcomes include Expanded Prostate Index Composite Short Form (EPIC-26), International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS), and EQ-5D-5L. This study is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05613023) and is ongoing.
FINDINGS: Between Sept 9, 2022, and July 31, 2025, 1166 participants were recruited and randomly assigned (583 per group). The median age was 72·7 years (IQR 67·7-76·5). 18 patients did not receive radiotherapy; a further 60 (17 assigned to P-SBRT, 43 assigned to PPN-SBRT) did not receive allocated radiotherapy, mostly where planning constraints were not met. This analysis includes 555 patients receiving P-SBRT and 511 patients receiving PPN-SBRT who had completed acute follow-up. Median follow-up was 13·8 months (IQR 7·8-21·0). 118 (21·3%) of 555 patients receiving P-SBRT and 143 (28·0%) of 511 receiving PPN-SBRT had grade 2 or worse gastrointestinal events within 12 weeks (difference 6·7 percentage points [95% CI 1·6-11·9]; p=0·011; odds ratio [OR] 1·44 [95% CI 1·09-1·91]). This included grade 3 events in eight (1·4%) patients treated with P-SBRT and 11 (2·2%) treated with PPN-SBRT, and a grade 4 event in one (0·2%) patient treated with P-SBRT. 223 (40·2%) of 555 patients receiving P-SBRT and 183 (35·8%) of 511 receiving PPN-SBRT had grade 2 or worse genitourinary events (difference -4·4 percentage points [-10·2 to 1·5]; p=0·14; OR 0·83 [0·65-1·06]). This included grade 3 events in seven (1·3%) patients treated with P-SBRT and two (0·4%) treated with PPN-SBRT (no grade 4 events). Genitourinary and gastrointestinal adverse events peaked at 2 weeks and were low and similar between groups at 12 weeks. There were no treatment-related deaths. More patients receiving PPN-SBRT had important decreases in bowel function on 4-week EPIC-26 (208 [54·9%] of 379 receiving P-SBRT, 239 [65·5%] of 365 receiving PPN-SBRT). The proportion of patients reporting moderate or severe urinary symptoms on IPSS at 4 weeks was similar in those receiving P-SBRT (312 [72·4%] of 431) and those receiving PPN-SBRT (284 [71·9%] of 395), as were 4-week decreases in overall health score on EQ-5D-5L (-3·2 [99% CI -4·8 to -1·6] for P-SBRT and -2·5 [-4·1 to -0·9] for PPN-SBRT).
INTERPRETATION: P-SBRT and PPN-SBRT for patients with high-risk prostate cancer were deliverable in an international multicentre trial. PPN-SBRT increased gastrointestinal but not genitourinary adverse events. Side-effects diminished rapidly, with no difference by 12 weeks. Follow-up continues for late adverse events and cancer control, which are essential for confirming a role for PPN-SBRT in this setting.
FUNDING: Prostate Cancer UK.

43043065.title: Molecular Features Underlying Discordance Between Clinical and Genomic Risk Stratification in Localized Prostate Cancer in Over 280, 000 Patients.
43043065.author: Zelefsky MJ
43043065.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Although the Decipher Genomic Classifier (GC) improves risk stratification beyond standard National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) risk groups, distinct clinical discordance exists between them. Herein, we interrogate specific adverse molecular features (AMFs) associated with genomic upgrading/downgrading relative to clinical risk and evaluate their overall long-term prognostic impact on treated patients.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: The specific prevalence of four separate AMFs (TP53 status, PTEN inactivation, lower androgen receptor [AR] activity, and RB1 loss) was evaluated across GC and NCCN risk groups using biopsy data from 287,145 patients. Prognostic associations with distant metastasis (DM) were fully assessed in 15,109 patients with NCCN high and very high-risk disease.
RESULTS: Decipher re-classified 21% of NCCN low and favorable intermediate-risk patients as high risk, while 33% of NCCN high-risk patients were GC-lower risk. AMF prevalence associated more strongly with GC than NCCN groups. TP53 mutant-like status, PTEN inactivation, and lower AR activity were associated with NCCN-GC discordance. Within the study cohort, a high GC score was associated with significantly increased risk of DM; AMFs independently predicted DM. Patients with at least one adverse AMF and a GC score >0.60 had a predicted 5-year DM probability of 17-25%, compared to 5% for those with favorable molecular profiles and a GC score ≤0.60.
CONCLUSIONS: Individual AMFs are associated with the discordance between NCCN and GC risk classifications. In patients with NCCN high-risk disease, the GC score serves as a primary prognostic driver, while AMF profiling provides additive risk stratification within specific clinical GC strata.

43046617.title: Immune protection against anogenital HPV in Rwandan women with and without HIV following the introduction of quadrivalent HPV vaccination.
43046617.author: Castle PE
43046617.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Prophylactic human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines have demonstrated population effectiveness in preventing cervical cancer. Evidence for protection of women with HIV (WWH) is lacking. In 2011, Rwanda introduced quadrivalent HPV vaccination nationally, primarily targeting girls in grade 6, providing an opportunity to evaluate its long-term effectiveness in WWH compared to women without HIV (WWoH).
METHODS: Data from 3,058 of 3,148 (97.1%) Rwandan women with complete results from four sub-cohorts recruited and enrolled were analyzed: 769 WWoH born before 1996, 755 WWoH born 1996 or more recently, 773 WWH born before 1996, and 761 WWH born 1996 or more recently. We tested vaginal and anal specimens for high-risk HPV genotypes. We used self-report of HPV vaccination and measured anti-HPV16 antibodies levels by HPV16 VLP ELISA as HPV vaccination proxies to examine the protective effects, using logistic regression, of HPV vaccination on vaginal and/or anal (combined, "anogenital") HPV16 and/or HPV18 (HPV16/18).
RESULTS: Self-reported HPV vaccination (vs. not) (adjusted odds ratio (aOR)=2.71, 95%CI=2.29-3.21) was most strongly positively, and WWH (vs. WWoH) (aOR=0.68, 95%CI=0.60-0.78) was most strongly negatively, associated with higher anti-HPV16 antibody levels. Anogenital HPV16/18 prevalence decreased from 11.0% to 2.5% in those with the lowest to highest quartile of anti-HPV16 antibody levels, respectively (ptrend<0.001). The highest quartile of anti-HPV16 antibody levels was associated with lower anogenital HPV16/18 (aOR=0.23, 95%CI=0.13-0.38); similar associations were observed for the highest quartile in WWH (aOR=0.23; 95%CI=0.12-0.46) as in WWoH (aOR=0.24, 95%CI=0.10-0.58).
CONCLUSION: WWH who were likely vaccinated against HPV vaccination had lower prevalence of anogenital HPV16/18.

43063921.title: Base Editing of Hematopoietic Stem Cells Corrects Gain-of-Function Mutations in APDS.
43063921.author: Orf K
43063921.abstract: Activated phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta syndrome 1 and 2 (APDS1, APDS2) are rare gain-of-function inborn errors of immunity (IEI) leading to recurrent severe infections, bronchiectasis, lymphoproliferation and lymphoma. APDS1 and APDS2 are caused by mutations in PIK3CD and PIK3R1 respectively, which together encode the subunits of the phosphoinositide 3-kinase  enzyme (PI3K). The only curative therapy is allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (alloHSCT), which requires a suitable donor and incurs a significant risk of morbidity and mortality. An adenine base editing strategy was developed to target the most frequent point mutations in APDS1 (p.E1021K, c.3061G>A; ~90% of patients) and APDS2 (c.1425+1G > A; ~50% of patients). Highly efficient correction of the pathogenic point mutation was achieved in patient T cells and hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) and associated with functional restoration of PI3K signaling, rescue of the activation-induced cell death phenotype and, in APDS2, abrogated expression of the pathogenic splice isoform. Edited HSCs maintained pluripotency and achieved long-term engraftment in immunodeficient mice. A healthy control:APDS1 mixed chimera mouse model suggested that 75% wild-type engraftment generated a wild-type phenotype with respect to T and B cell dysfunction and lymphoproliferation, and thus similar editing efficiencies would be predicted to improve patient clinical phenotype. Together, these data demonstrate successful application of base editing to a gain-of-function IEI, with potential for application in other diseases.

43063920.title: FLT3 Mutations in Myelodysplastic Syndromes and Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemia: A Multi-Center Analysis.
43063920.author: Rodríguez-Sevilla JJ
43063920.abstract: FLT3 mutations are established high-risk drivers in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), but their role in myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) and chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML) remains poorly defined. We assembled 115 patients with FLT3-mutant MDS (n=63) or CMML (n=52) across six academic institutions and compared clinicogenomic features and outcomes with FLT3-wildtype controls using propensity score matching and multivariable modeling. FLT3-mutant MDS and CMML displayed a proliferative phenotype, with higher white blood cell counts, increased frequency of CMML-2, and significantly higher rates of AML transformation. FLT3-mutant MDS was enriched for signaling co-mutations, such as NRAS, PTPN11, and CBL, whereas FLT3-mutant CMML showed frequent co-mutation with ASXL1 and SRSF2. FLT3 mutations were independently associated with inferior survival in both entities. After matching, FLT3-mutant MDS had worse median overall survival (OS: 19.9 vs 44.2 months, p=0.046) and leukemia-free survival (LFS: 13.8 vs 37.1 months, p=0.023). In CMML, median OS was 30.4 vs 67.2 months (p=0.017) and LFS 17.2 vs 65.6 months (p=0.014). FLT3-TKD was associated with more favorable outcomes than FLT3-ITD. FLT3-targeted therapy was associated with longer survival in unadjusted comparisons (median OS 14.3 vs 45.9 months in MDS; 20.6 vs 35.0 months in CMML), although this association was attenuated and no longer statistically significant after accounting for immortal time bias introduced from variable treatment initiation timing (adjusted time-dependent HR 0.66, MDS; 0.64, CMML). These findings support early identification of FLT3-mutant MDS and CMML and highlight the need for prospective studies evaluating early therapeutic intervention in this high-risk molecular subset.

43063919.title: STI-8591: A Novel FLT3 Inhibitor Targeting Resistant FLT3 Mutations and central nervous system Leukemia.
43063919.author: Zhang Y
43063919.abstract: FLT3 mutations presented in 30% of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients and correlate with high relapse rates and poor prognosis. Resistance mutations and central nervous system (CNS) involvement remain major challenges despite clinical FLT3 inhibitors. This study evaluated the preclinical efficacy and safety of STI-8591, a novel kinase inhibitor, in FLT3-mutant (FLT3 mut）AML, focusing on the FLT3-ITD-F691L resistance mutation and CNS leukemia models to support clinical translation. STI-8591 was tested in FLT3 mut human AML cell lines (MV4-11, MOLM-13), murine Ba/F3 cells expressing various FLT3 mutants (D835Y, ITD-D835Y, ITD-F691L), and primary AML blasts. Effects on proliferation, apoptosis, cell cycle, colony formation, and FLT3 signaling were assessed. Five in vivo models were used: Ba/F3-FLT3 mutant xenograft, MllPTD/WT:Flt3ITD/ITD transgenic, MOLM-13 CDX, CNS leukemia CDX, and chemoresistant PDX models. Pharmacokinetics and toxicology were evaluated in mice, rats, and dogs. In vitro, STI-8591 potently inhibited proliferation of FLT3 mut cell lines (IC50: 1.94-10.82 nM) and primary blasts (de novo IC50: 3.37-160.50 nM; relapsed/refractory IC50: 12.4-800.3 nM), induced G0/G1 arrest and apoptosis, and blocked FLT3/STAT5/AKT/ERK phosphorylation. In patient-derived CD34⁺blasts, 40 nM STI-8591 reduced colony formation by 94%. Orally administered STI-8591 (3-30 mg/kg) significantly suppressed leukemia progression and prolonged survival in all models. Notably, it maintained efficacy against the FLT3-ITD-F691L gatekeeper mutation, outperforming Gilteritinib, and showed activity in CNS leukemia and chemoresistant PDX models. PK/toxicology studies demonstrated favorable profiles without unexpected adverse effects. STI-8591 is a promising therapeutic agent for FLT3 mut AML, including resistant subtypes and CNS involvement.

43063918.title: Systematic Review Supporting the American Society of Hematology Practice Guidelines on the Management of Myelofibrosis.
43063918.author: Hasan B
43063918.abstract: Myelofibrosis (MF) is a Philadelphia-negative clonal disorder of hematopoietic stem cells associated with substantial clinical practice variation. The American Society of Hematology (ASH) convened a guideline panel that prioritized ten clinical questions to inform evidence-based recommendations. We performed a comprehensive systematic review of MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane databases, and Scopus through January 2025 to identify studies that addressed the ten clinical questions. Meta-analyses were performed where feasible. Two reviewers independently selected and appraised studies. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. Of 3,007 records screened, 43 unique studies met inclusion criteria for the ten questions. Extended molecular testing identified high-risk mutations (ASXL1, EZH2, SRSF2, IDH1/2) that were significantly associated with decreased overall survival (hazard ratios ranging 1.5-4.5). JAK inhibitors improved spleen and symptom responses in symptomatic lower-risk MF and in patients with anemia, with momelotinib improving transfusion independence. However, survival effects were not clearly demonstrated and hematologic toxicity remained common. Evidence for treating asymptomatic high-risk patients with JAK inhibitors was particularly limited. Early allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation was associated with higher early mortality but improved long-term survival compared with delayed transplantation. Pretransplant JAK inhibitor exposure did not significantly affect mortality, GVHD, or graft failure. Evidence for interferon, aspirin, and iron chelation was limited and largely indirect. The certainty of evidence was very low or low across nearly all outcomes.

43063917.title: Increasing Donor Age Remains Associated with Adverse Transplant Outcomes in the Post-Transplant Cyclophosphamide Era.
43063917.author: Xie Y
43063917.abstract: Advanced donor age is an established determinant of worse outcomes in allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) using methotrexate/calcineurin inhibitor (CNI)-based graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) prophylaxis. But recent analyses of overlapping populations receiving post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy)-based GVHD prophylaxis have reported different estimates of the magnitude and donor-type dependence of this association. Using a Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research (CIBMTR) cohort, we analyzed 5,873 patients with acute leukemia or myelodysplastic syndrome undergoing first allogeneic HCT using matched unrelated (MUD) or haploidentical donors with PTCy. Outcomes included overall survival (OS), GVHD-free/relapse-free survival (GRFS), relapse, non-relapse mortality (NRM), acute GVHD, and chronic GVHD. We applied a hybrid analytical framework combining machine learning-based survival modeling (XGBoost) and multivariable Cox regression using generalized propensity score weighting. Considering MUD and haploidentical donors, each 10-year increase in donor age was associated with inferior OS (HR, 1.076; 95%CI, 1.030-1.124; p=0.001) and GRFS (HR, 1.098; 95%CI, 1.060-1.138; p<0.001) and higher risks of NRM and acute and chronic GVHD. Donor age was not significantly associated with relapse, and donor age-by-donor type interactions were not statistically significant. Model-estimated 24-month OS decreased from 63.3% at donor age 25 to 59.4% at age 45, and GRFS from 43.8% to 37.1%. Our findings provide an alternative characterization of donor-age associations in PTCy-based HCT and suggest that increasing donor age remains associated with adverse transplant outcomes without clear evidence of different effects between MUD and haploidentical donors.

43063518.title: Navitoclax and Venetoclax with Chemotherapy for Relapsed/Refractory ALL in Children and Young Adults.
43063518.author: Del Bufalo F
43063518.abstract: Despite improving survival rates, a significant number of children, adolescents and young adults (CAYA) with relapsed/refractory acute lymphoblastic leukemia (r/r ALL) still die from disease. This calls for new drugs combination to reinduce complete remissions (CR) and enable consolidation. B-cell lymphoma (BCL) family proteins have a key role in regulating the blast apoptotic response to chemotherapy-induced cell damage and the combination of the BCL-2 and BCL-XL/BCL-2 inhibitors (venetoclax [VEN] and navitoclax [NAV], respectively) with chemotherapy could revert the resistance observed in r/r ALL. We retrospectively collected data of NAV/VEN, combined with chemotherapy, in 30 CAYA with advanced, R/R, either B-ALL (n=17) or T-ALL (n=13), treated under compassionate use, in 5 European centers. NAV and VEN (median number of cycles 1, range 1-3) were administered over 28 days. The most common toxicity was hematologic: overall, 93% of the patients developed grade 3-4 neutropenia, 83% grade 3-4 anemia and 83% grade 3-4 thrombocytopenia. No fatal adverse event was recorded. The overall response rate (CR/CRi/PR) was 71% for the B-ALL (12/17 patients) and 50% (6/12) for the T-ALL cohort, allowing, respectively, 11 and 4 patients to receive further consolidation. Six B-ALL patients and 2 T-ALL patients are alive and maintain response, with a median follow-up of 25 (0,6 - 38) and 8 months (0.5-47), respectively. All patients who did not receive consolidation ultimately relapsed and died. Our experience underlines the strong potential of NAV/VEN plus conventional chemotherapy to reinduce complete remission in heavily pretreated and refractory CAYA with either B- or T-ALL.

43053710.title: Reduced intensity hematopoietic cell transplant using best available donor and post-transplant cyclophosphamide is safe and curative for transfusion-dependent thalassemia.
43053710.author: Ktena YP
43053710.abstract: Over 300,000 live births annually are affected by hemoglobinopathies worldwide. Of these, transfusion-dependent thalassemias (TDTs) result in severe phenotypes that significantly impact quality of life, shorten life expectancy, and incur high lifetime healthcare costs driven by recurrent transfusions and chelation therapy. Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT) is curative but limited by donor availability, regimen toxicity, graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), and transplant-related mortality. We present our single-center experience of TDT patients who underwent allo-HCT using a reduced-intensity conditioning (RIC) regimen (anti-thymocyte globulin, fludarabine, cyclophosphamide, total body irradiation) and posttransplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy)-based GVHD prophylaxis. Twenty-five consecutive children and young adults (ages 2-23 years, median 9) with TDT (beta-thalassemia major n=21, hemoglobin E-beta thalassemia n=3, hemoglobin D-beta thalassemia n=1) underwent HCT from July 2013 to November 2024. Bone marrow was the most common graft source (n=23, 92% of all patients), and haploidentical donors were the most common donor type (n=19, 76% of all patients). Neutrophil and platelet recovery occurred at median 21 days (range 13-38) and 26 days (range 16-88), respectively. Five patients (20%) developed grade I-II acute GVHD; none developed grade III-IV acute GVHD. Two (8%) developed mild chronic GVHD. At a median follow-up of 5.6 years (range 0.7-10), 5-year overall survival was 100%, transfusion-free survival 96%, and thalassemia-free-GVHD-free survival 96% - one patient experienced near-complete loss of donor chimerism with return of the TDT phenotype. Our RIC platform with best-available donor and PTCy-based GVHD prophylaxis significantly reduces post-HCT complications while providing durable transfusion independence, offering a proven, accessible, curative option for TDT.

43053705.title: Severe and fatal central nervous system toxicity after fludarabine, thiotepa and melphalan conditioning for allogeneic stem cell transplantation.
43053705.author: Schonewille P
43053705.abstract: Neurological complications (NC) are a known risk after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT). In routine clinical care, we observed unexpected severe noninfectious central nervous system (CNS) events following conditioning with fludarabine, thiotepa and melphalan (Flu-Thio-Mel). To assess the potential association between NC and Flu-Thio-Mel conditioning, we conducted a systematic retrospective evaluation of the frequency, type, location and etiology of NC in adult patients who received αβTCR+/CD19+-depleted allo-HSCT. Only NC considered conditioningrelated, based on clinical and diagnostic findings, were included. Outcomes were compared between patients receiving Flu-Thio-Mel (N=55) and patients receiving fludarabine and busulfan (Flu-Bu; N=47) as conditioning regimen for allo-HSCT. Overall, NC were frequent in both cohorts (31% after Flu-Thio-Mel and 30% after Flu-Bu) and most often clinically mild. Peripheral neuropathy was the most common manifestation. In contrast, CNS toxicity was observed exclusively in the Flu-Thio-Mel cohort (n=7), presenting as fatal leukoencephalopathy (n=3, CTCAE grade 5), severe encephalomyelopathy (n=2, CTCAE grade 3-4), and myeloneuropathy (n=2, CTCAE grade 2). Older age, impaired renal function and higher fludarabine exposure may have increased susceptibility to Flu-Thio-Mel-associated CNS toxicity. The occurrence of severe CNS toxicity (CTCAE grade 3-5) in 9% of patients after Flu-Thio-Mel warrants caution and further evaluation of this conditioning regimen, particularly in vulnerable patients.

43053704.title: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation after CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy in children and adults with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia: a GoCART coalition study on behalf of the PDWP, ALWP, and CTIWP of the EBMT.
43053704.author: Ottaviano G
43053704.abstract: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) can rescue B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) recurring after CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor T cells (CAR19 T cells). However, in patients at high risk of relapse, the indication for and timing of consolidative HSCT are controversial. We retrieved data on 112 patients who received an HSCT at a median of 6.1 months after CAR19 T-cell infusion. Indication for subsequent HSCT were: (I) Rescue in 72 (64%) patients for disease recurrence; (II) Pre-emptive in 21 (19%) for loss of B-cell aplasia; (III) Consolidative in 19 patients (17%). The 2-year post-transplant Leukemia-Free Survival (LFS) was 54% and the 2-year cumulative incidence of relapse was 32%. Children had better LFS than adults (63% vs 38%). Older age was associated with inferior LFS (HR per 10-year increase 1.30; p= 0.01) and patients receiving a rescue HSCT had a significantly lower 2-year LFS (41%), compared to pre-emptive (74%) and consolidative HSCT (78%), respectively (p=0.002). Haploidentical donor was also associated with inferior LFS (HR: 2.21 95%CI: 1.15-4.25, p=0.02). This "real-world" study corroborates the need to identify patients at higher risk of relapse and optimization of strategies to improve outcome in patients with R/R B-ALL receiving CD19-directed CAR T cells.

43050686.title: Real World Comparison of Asciminib Versus Ponatinib in Chronic Myeloid Leukemia with Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
43050686.author: Perusini MA
43050686.abstract: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) has an excellent prognosis with tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs); however, approximately 40-50% of patients discontinue at least one TKI because of resistance or intolerance. While Ponatinib (PON) is highly effective against resistant disease, Asciminib (ASC) offers robust efficacy with favorable tolerability profile. In the absence of randomized head-to-head trials, we compared outcomes of ASC versus PON using propensity score-matched (PSM) analysis. We conducted a real-world analysis of 762 CML patients previously treated with ≥1 TKI (ASC, n=451; PON, n=311), from an international multicenter cohort. PSM generated 139 balanced pairs after adjusting for age, prior TKI exposure, cardiovascular history, ABL kinase domain mutations, and reason for prior TKI failure. The primary endpoints, evaluated in the matched cohort, were 12-month failure-free survival (FFS) and event-free survival (EFS). ASC was associated with similar molecular response rates and FFS to PON, while EFS was significantly longer with ASC, likely reflecting its more favorable tolerability and lower rate of discontinuation due to intolerance. The difference in EFS was particularly pronounced among patients treated for prior TKI intolerance and in lower-risk subgroups. A sensitivity analysis restricted to patients naïve to both agents (117 matched pairs) confirmed the EFS difference (12-month EFS, 88.6% vs 73.2%; HR 2.48; p=0.002). ASC was associated with similar molecular response and FFS outcomes to PON These findings suggest that ASC was associated with similar real-world molecular response and FFS outcomes to PON, while EFS was longer with ASC, largely driven by differences in treatment discontinuation related to intolerance. ASC may represent an attractive option for patients with prior TKI intolerance, while PON remains an important treatment option for patients with resistant disease.

43046952.title: Combined inhibition of BCL2 activity and CD28 signaling to prevent graft-versus-host disease.
43046952.author: Chen H
43046952.abstract: Post-transplantation cyclophosphamide (PTCy)-based prophylaxis has become one of the most widely used strategies to prevent graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), particularly after HLA-haploidentical hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT). Well-tolerated GVHD prophylaxis regimens beyond PTCy are needed, because adverse events associated with Cy administration, such as cardiac toxicity, remain a safety concern. Costimulation blockade using abatacept (ABA) is an established complementary strategy to improve GVHD prevention without a calcineurin inhibitor. Here, we investigated venetoclax (VEN), a selective B-cell leukemia/lymphoma 2 (BCL-2) inhibitor, as a candidate partner with ABA to prevent GVHD. In a murine MHC-haploidentical HCT model, we demonstrate that prevention of GVHD with a combination of short-term VEN and CD28 costimulation blockade using ABA (VEN+ABA) was comparable to that with Cy+ABA and superior to that with Cy monotherapy, while maintaining GVL effects. Flow cytometry analysis revealed a higher regulatory T (Treg)/conventional T (Tcon) ratio with the VEN+ABA combination compared to Cy+ABA. Using donor CD8+ alloreactive TCR-transgenic T cells, we show that the VEN+ABA combination produced a prominent cleaved caspase-3 signature only in allo-activated T cells, and cells from the spleen at day 9 after HCT with VEN+ABA did not respond after ex vivo CD3/CD28 stimulation. Collectively, our study supports a VEN+ABA GVHD prophylaxis strategy associated with preferential apoptosis of alloreactive T cells while preserving GVL activity to replace alkylator-based prophylaxis.

43045694.title: Impact of race/ethnicity, donor and recipient age, and donor on survival after allogeneic transplant in the post-transplant cyclophosphamide era.
43045694.author: Herr MM

43038184.title: Microbiota-derived short-chain fatty acids control cGVHD development by regulating antibody production.
43038184.author: Wolfe AE
43038184.abstract: Chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) contributes substantially to morbidity and mortality in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients. Microbe-derived short-chain fatty acids (SCFA) exert diverse local effects on the intestinal mucosa. We previously reported that a relative deficiency of SCFA in the circulation of transplant patients was associated with an increased incidence of cGVHD. We therefore hypothesized that circulating SCFA were unrecognized immunomodulators, generating protective effects after transplantation. We examined the role of SCFA butyrate and propionate in mouse models of cGVHD and now report that systemic administration of either butyrate or propionate mitigates cGVHD and improves survival. Exogenous SCFA treatment reduced pathogenic hyperexpanded B cells and recipient-specific IgA in the circulation, as well as decreasing the total alloantibody pool, defined using rapid extracellular antigen profiling (REAP). Our findings uncover a mechanism by which the intestinal microbiome plays a role in regulating antibody-dependent cGVHD pathogenesis and has implications for other antibody-mediated pathologies.

43038176.title: CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM GRAFT VERSUS HOST DISEASE PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: MECHANISTIC PATHWAYS AND THERAPEUTIC TARGETS.
43038176.author: Rayasam A
43038176.abstract: The development of graft versus host disease (GVHD) in the central nervous system (CNS) is a recognized complication that can lead to significant morbidity and mortality in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients. In this article, we describe clinical manifestations and elucidate some of the diagnostic challenges associated with this disease entity. We then summarize new experimental insights that have emerged largely from pre-clinical murine studies that have investigated the pathophysiology of CNS GVHD. We delineate the vascular and lymphatic systems that regulate ingress and egress of soluble mediators and cellular populations, thereby functioning as specialized barriers that shield the brain under normal homeostatic conditions, and how these barriers are disrupted during GVHD-induced peripheral immune dysregulation. We also review pre-clinical studies that have uncovered mechanistic neuroinflammatory pathways involving cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α), cell surface receptors (type 2 cannabinoid receptor, colony stimulating factor-1 receptor) expressed on adaptive and innate immune cells, and antibiotic-induced gastrointestinal tract dysbiosis that have pathophysiological roles in this disorder. In addition, we provide evidence derived from these pre-clinical studies that the therapeutic targeting of individual pathways to attenuate CNS GVHD does not necessarily produce concordant responses in peripheral GVHD target organs, highlighting that the brain is a compartmentalized tissue site with a distinct microenvironment and supporting a more nuanced view of GVHD biology across CNS and non-CNS regions. Finally, we examine alternate therapeutic strategies to restore barrier integrity and thereby reduce T cell trafficking into the CNS to attenuate GVHD-associated neuroinflammation.

43038169.title: Regenerative Stress Contributes to Higher Clonal Hematopoiesis with Myelodysplastic Features in Sickle Cell Disease Mice.
43038169.author: Chi M
43038169.abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) affects millions globally, causing significant lifelong morbidity and early death. As childhood mortality is reduced and SCD patients are surviving to adulthood, increased risk of hematological malignancy (HM) is becoming evident. Risk of therapy-related myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS)/acute myeloid leukemia, following gene therapy or hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) is also higher in SCD. The specific pathobiology that predisposes to HM is necessary to address, since survival has improved and gene therapy and HSCT are being increasingly used. We modelled the increased risk of HM in humanized SCD mice, compared to age-, sex- and strain-matched normal counterparts. We serially monitored hematopoiesis in blood and bone marrow up to 1-year-of-age and performed highly sensitive, error-corrected deep sequencing of 450 MDS/HM-associated genes. Unlike controls, SCD mice showed an 'ageing-like' phenotype with premature development of myeloid-biased hematopoiesis and hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (HSPC) mutational profile characteristic of aged mice/humans. Furthermore, a high proportion of SCD mice developed hematopoiesis with dysplastic features reminiscent of MDS morphology and higher clonal hematopoiesis burden. Imposition of regenerative stress by serial HSCT further increased HSPC mutational burden, resulting in evolution/expansion of clones harboring oncogenic driver mutations. Our study indicates that increased HSC regenerative stress, imposed either by chronic erythropoietic demand or via autologous HSCT in SCD increases the risk of developing clonal hematopoiesis and MDS-like features. Our study provides insights into a mechanism underlying increased risk of HM in this non-malignant hematological disorder, and suggests that early intervention with curative therapies may circumvent this risk.

43037096.title: New diagnostic criteria can inflate myelodysplastic syndrome survival estimates.
43037096.author: Giguère P
43037096.abstract: Survival in oncology is reported to be improving, often attributed to better detection, diagnostics and treatments. However, the impact of disease reclassification is largely ignored despite the potential for bias in historical comparisons. We used the Molecular International Prognostic Scoring System cohort to estimate the effect of introducing a Myelodysplastic Syndrome/ Acute Myeloid Leukemia (MDS/AML) category to the classification of Myelodysplastic Syndrome. Survival was compared between: (1) "MDS-2016" including all patients with ≤ 19% blasts and (2) "MDS-2022" restricted to patients with < 10% blasts, the latter simulating a cohort without MDS/AML. Median survival increased from 3.4 years (95%CI 3.1-3.9) to 4.3 years (95%CI 4.0-4.6) and 5-year survival from 39.0% (95%CI 36.5-41.6%) to 43.6% (95%CI 40.8-46.6%) all favouring MDS-2022. Thus, reclassification alone can produce a clinically meaningful apparent improvement in survival. Consideration of this effect is essential for interest-holders. Replication in other datasets and for other diseases is warranted.

43035765.title: Upfront venetoclax plus quizartinib with low-dose cytarabine or azacitidine in older unfit patients with acute myeloid leukemia: the phase I/II VEN-A-QUI trial.
43035765.author: Bergua JM
43035765.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Many older patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) are ineligible for intensive chemotherapy. Quizartinib, an oral, selective, FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3) inhibitor is approved in combination with intensive chemotherapy for patients with newly diagnosed (ND) FLT3-internal tandem duplication (ITD)-positive AML. Quizartinib efficacy and safety in combination with venetoclax plus either azacitidine (VEN-AZA-Quiz) or low-dose cytarabine (VEN-LDAC-Quiz) were investigated in patients ineligible for intensive chemotherapy.
METHODS: The phase I/II, multicenter, prospective, open-label, VEN-A-QUI trial enrolled patients aged ≥ 60 years with ND FLT3-ITD-positive or -negative AML.
PHASE I: patients were assigned to parallel VEN-AZA-Quiz or VEN-LDAC-Quiz dose-escalation cohorts.
PHASE II: patients were randomized 1:1 to VEN-AZA-Quiz or VEN-LDAC-Quiz. Primary endpoints were the determination of quizartinib recommended phase II dose (RP2D; phase I) and composite complete remission (CRc) rate (phase II).
RESULTS: Fourteen and 60 patients received treatment in phase I and II, respectively. The quizartinib RP2D was 60 mg/day for VEN-AZA-Quiz and 40 mg/day for VEN-LDAC-Quiz. In phase II, CRc by Cycle 4 was achieved in 18/31 patients (58.1%) receiving VEN-AZA-Quiz and 15/29 (51.7%) receiving VEN-LDAC-Quiz (p = 0.80). Median overall survival (OS) was 16.9 months and 8.9 months for VEN-AZA-Quiz and VEN-LDAC-Quiz, respectively (p = 0.81), with 3-year OS rates of 22.6% and 27.6%. Overall, a high CRc rate (10/13, 76.9%) and median OS (29.3 months) was observed in FLT3-ITD-positive patients. Median OS was 32 months for de novo AML and 7.5 months for secondary AML (p < 0.001). The most common adverse events were infectious and hematologic toxicity.
CONCLUSIONS: VEN-AZA-Quiz and VEN-LDAC-Quiz regimens demonstrated clinical activity in patients with ND AML aged ≥ 60 years ineligible for intense chemotherapy, particularly in patients with de novo AML, with an acceptable safety profile.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04687761.

43063370.title: Effect of a Multidisciplinary Intervention on Fatigue in Lymphoma Survivors With Persistent Fatigue: A Randomized Controlled Trial (the REFUEL trial).
43063370.author: Bøhn SH
43063370.abstract:
PURPOSE: Persistent fatigue is a prevalent, complex, and distressing late effect among lymphoma survivors. We examined the effect of a multidisciplinary intervention on fatigue among lymphoma survivors with persistent fatigue.
METHODS: Lymphoma survivors with persistent fatigue (moderate to severe fatigue ≥6 months) were randomly assigned to usual care (n = 75) or a 12-week multidisciplinary intervention (n = 75). The intervention consisted of patient education, physical exercise, a cognitive-behavioral therapy-based program, and nutritional counseling. Total fatigue was assessed by the Chalder Fatigue Questionnaire (range, 0-33) 3 months after random assignment (T1; primary outcome) and at 6 (T2) and 9 (T3) months after random assignment (secondary outcomes). Other secondary outcomes were functioning and global health status/quality of life (QoL) assessed by European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer QoL Questionnaire-C30. Effects were analyzed with baseline-adjusted linear mixed models for repeated measures.
RESULTS: Compared with usual care, the intervention group reported significantly lower total fatigue at T1 (between-group difference [BGD], -3.5 [95% CI, -5.4 to -1.6]; P < .001). Secondary outcome analyses indicated that total fatigue remained lower in the intervention group at T2 (BGD, -2.4 [95% CI, -4.4 to -0.5]), but not at T3 (BGD, -0.9 [95% CI, -3.0 to 1.2]). At T1, secondary outcome analyses indicated positive intervention effects on physical (BGD, 3.8 [95% CI, 0.2 to 7.3]) and role functioning (BGD, 9.2 [95% CI, 0.9 to 17.5]) and global health status/QoL (BGD, 9.5 [95% CI, 3.5 to 15.4]), but not on social (BGD, -0.1 [95% CI, -7.4 to 7.3]), emotional (BGD, 5.6 [95% CI, 0.0 to 11.3]), or cognitive functioning (BGD, 3.5 [95% CI, -3.3 to 10.2]).
CONCLUSION: A multidisciplinary intervention improved fatigue among lymphoma survivors with persistent fatigue. The effect appeared to be maintained 6 months after random assignment but dissipated at 9 months.

43063368.title: Alectinib as Neoadjuvant Treatment in Potentially Resectable Stage III Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase-Positive Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: ALNEO Phase II Trial (GOIRC-01-2020-ML42316).
43063368.author: Leonetti A
43063368.abstract:
PURPOSE: Stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a heterogeneous disease with no single definitive therapeutic approach. The role of neoadjuvant tyrosine kinase inhibitors in stage III ALK-positive NSCLC remains unknown. The ALNEO study evaluated the activity and safety of perioperative alectinib in this population.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: ALNEO is an open-label, single-arm, multicenter phase II study enrolling treatment-naïve patients with potentially resectable stage III ALK-positive NSCLC. Patients received neoadjuvant alectinib 600 mg twice daily for 8 weeks, followed by surgery and adjuvant alectinib for up to 96 weeks. The primary end point was major pathologic response (MPR; ≤10% residual viable tumor cells) assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included pathologic complete response (pCR), objective response rate (ORR), event-free survival (EFS), disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and safety.
RESULTS: From May 2021 to July 2024, 33 patients were enrolled. The median age was 62 years (range, 33-79), 70% were female, and 52% were never smokers. Clinical stage was IIIA in 64% and IIIB in 36%. All patients completed neoadjuvant treatment, and 28 (85%) underwent surgery, most commonly lobectomy (75%). R0 resection was achieved in 24 (86%). MPR was observed in 14 patients (42%; 95% CI, 26 to 61), including four pCRs (12%; 95% CI, 3 to 28). ORR was 67%. Adjuvant treatment was initiated in 26 (79%) patients. After a median follow-up of 26.8 months, median EFS, DFS, and OS were not reached; six patients (18%) experienced disease recurrence. Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 9% and 27% of patients during neoadjuvant and adjuvant treatment, respectively.
CONCLUSION: The ALNEO study met its primary end point, suggesting perioperative alectinib as a feasible and active approach in potentially resectable stage III ALK-positive NSCLC.

43058221.title: Expansion and cytotoxicity of mucosal CAR(+) T cells in enterocolitis associated with BCMA CAR-T cell therapy.
43058221.author: Sainz TP
43058221.abstract: Ciltacabtagene autoleucel (cilta-cel) is a B cell maturation-antigen-targeting chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell product approved for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma treatment. Previously reported cases of post-cilta-cel immune effector cell enterocolitis (IEC-EC) have been described as a severe diarrhea associated with clonal CAR T cell populations. Here we report nine cases of cilta-cel-associated IEC-EC with CAR T cell-positive (CAR+) infiltration in 158 cilta-cel-treated patients at MD Anderson Cancer Center (incidence of 5.1% at a 6-month landmark and 5.7% globally). Cilta-cel infiltration was the primary cause of IEC-EC, and all cases demonstrated monoclonal or oligoclonal T cell populations as measured by vector integration analysis, flow cytometry and T cell receptor sequencing. Patients with IEC-EC had 100-fold more CAR T cell persistence in the peripheral blood than patients without IEC-EC. RNA sequencing analysis revealed increased cytotoxic and inflammatory programs associated with the CAR+ infiltrates relative to controls. Clonal vector integration occurred in introns of highly expressed genes without evidence of vector-mediated mutagenesis. Candidate driver mutations were sparse and heterogeneous, distinguishing IEC-EC from peripheral T cell lymphoma following CAR T cell therapy. In sum, we find that IEC-EC pathology represents a distinct, duodenum-predominant, clonal lymphoproliferative disorder characterized by the infiltration of clonal CAR+ cytotoxic T cells into the gastrointestinal tract.

43053711.title: Integrating information across datasets to improve prognostic models for patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
43053711.author: Xie C
43053711.abstract: Accurate survival prediction is vital for guiding clinical decisions in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), especially for advancing precision medicine within its genomically heterogeneous subgroups. However, datasets that include both detailed clinical variables and genomic profiling are usually small. In contrast, large population-based datasets often lack multiomics data. This gap limits the development and validation of robust prognostic models in DLBCL. We developed a transfer-learning prognostic framework that leverages the external population-level information from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results program to the prognostic model for an individual-level clinical and genomic cohort. The proposed model is a Cox-model-based boosted regression with individual data for generalization and enhancement (BRIDGE-Cox) that increases predictive accuracy and reduces uncertainty. The BRIDGE-Cox model incorporates the International Prognostic Index (IPI) factors, with model training performed in the Reddy genomic dataset and external validation in an independent National Cancer Institute genomic dataset. Compared with conventional IPI-based and revised IPI-based Cox models, the BRIDGE-Cox model improved predictive performance for overall survival, achieving a higher concordance index (0.70 vs 0.66 and 0.63, respectively) and consistently higher time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curves for 2-, 3-, and 5- year survival prediction by using the repeated cross-validation in the Reddy dataset. Importantly, these gains were maintained within genomic subgroups. External validation confirmed the robustness and generalizability of the BRIDGE-Cox approach. By borrowing large populationlevel data, this model addresses key limitations of existing tools and enables more reliable risk stratification for patients with DLBCL, particularly in genomically defined subpopulations.

43053709.title: Outcomes associated with CD3xCD20 bispecific antibody therapies in relapsed/refractory transformed indolent lymphoma.
43053709.author: Stephan P
43053709.abstract: Transformed indolent non-Hodgkin lymphoma (tiNHL) has historically been associated with poor outcomes, particularly for patients with relapsed or refractory (R/R) disease. Although chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has improved prognosis, many patients lack access or experience relapse following treatment, highlighting the need for additional therapeutic strategies. CD3×CD20 bispecific antibodies (BsAbs) are active in R/R large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL), though data in tiNHL are limited. Here, we report the efficacy and safety of epcoritamab and glofitamab in patients with R/R tiNHL (N = 74) compared with those of patients with R/R de novo diffuse LBCL (DLBCL; N = 166) from 9 academic centers in the Collaborative US Bispecifics Consortium (CUBIC). With a median follow-up of 11.5 months, best overall response rate (ORR) and complete response rate (CRR) were comparable in tiNHL (50%/31%) vs de novo DLBCL (51%/34%). 12-month progression-free survival was 25% (95% confidence interval [CI], 15-39) for tiNHL vs 34% (95% CI, 27-43) for de novo DLBCL (HR, 1.15 [95% CI, 0.83-1.61]) and 12-month overall survival was 38% (95% CI, 26-55) for tiNHL vs 47% (95% CI, 39-56) for de novo DLBCL (HR, 1.08 [95% CI, 0.73-1.60]). No differences in toxicity were observed. Similar findings were found via a 1:1 propensity score matching statistical approach. In conclusion, our study revealed comparable efficacy and toxicity of BsAbs for patients with R/R tiNHL vs patients with R/R de novo DLBCL, supporting their use in this patient population.

43053707.author: Perry C
43053707.abstract: Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) is a curable malignancy with excellent long-term survival, shifting the focus of care toward survivorship challenges, including mental and functional health. This population-based retrospective cohort study evaluated the incidence, timing, and risk factors for mental and functional disorders (including fibromyalgia, irritable bowel syndrome, insomnia and related conditions) among young adult HL survivors in Israel compared with age- and sex-matched controls. Data was retrieved from the electronic medical database of Maccabi Healthcare Services, encompassing 1007 young (18-50 years) HL patients, diagnosed between 1995 and 2021, and 20140 controls, with a median follow-up of 12 years. Prior to HL diagnosis, mental or functional disorders were more prevalent among patients than controls (15.3% vs. 10.2%, p.

43053701.title: Characterization and impact of response to holding/bridging therapy in second-line large B-cell lymphoma patients treated with axicabtagene ciloleucel: a LYSA study from the French DESCAR-T registry.
43053701.author: Capes A
43053701.abstract: The optimal approach for holding or bridging therapy (H/BT) prior to second line axicabtagene ciloleucel (axi-cel) remains undefined, and the prognostic impact of response to H/BT remains debated. Here, we characterize real-world H/BT strategies and evaluate the impact of response on outcome following axi-cel infusion in the second-line setting for relapse or refractory (R/R) large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL). We included all adults with R/R LBCL within 12 months of first-line therapy who received axi-cel in the nationwide French DESCAR-T cohort (NCT04328298). The primary objective was to EFS between H/BT responders and nonresponders, as per Lugano criteria, using propensity score matching (PSM). Secondary objectives were to characterize H/BT modalities, corresponding responses, and to identify predictors of EFS at infusion. Among 566 patients included, 469 (83%) received chemotherapy-based H/BT, while 97 (17%) received a chemo-free approach, including no H/BT. Patients treated with chemotherapy-based H/BT had more advanced disease characteristics and exhibited inferior EFS compared to those receiving chemo-free approaches. After PSM, OS was significantly improved in responders versus non-responders (HR=0·70 [95% CI 0·51-0·96], p=0·0292), while the EFS benefit no longer reached statistical significance (HR=0·86 [95%CI 0·70-1·07], p=0·1739). Given that only patients ultimately receiving axi-cel were analyzed, the impact of H/BT response may have been underestimated. A predictive score combining response to H/BT, international prognostic index, LDH, and CRP at infusion identified two risk groups with significantly different EFS. In conclusion, H/BT response appears to be associated with axi-cel outcomes particularly when combined to inflammatory markers and residual LDH.

43053699.title: Preserving liposomal anthracycline exposure and reconsidering radiotherapy in frontline therapy of older adults with advanced-stage classical Hodgkin lymphoma. 43053698.title: The preanalytical phase in hematopathology: sampling as a critical step for an appropriate diagnosis. A position paper from the Italian Group of Haematopathology (GIE).
43053698.author: Lucioni M
43053698.abstract: Lymphoma diagnosis relies on morphological, immunophenotypical and molecular analyses of lesional tissue biopsies. Expert guidelines recommend surgical excision biopsy (SEB) of lymph nodes as the standard approach, as it provides adequate tissue for definitive diagnosis, accurate subtyping, and treatment selection, but core needle biopsy (CNB) is increasingly used in clinical practice because of its practical advantages. However, a critical analysis of most published series reveals that CNB may have lower diagnostic accuracy than SEB, with a high risk of inadequate/insufficient material and tissue artifacts, leading to non-definitive diagnoses and lymphoma subtype misclassification, which may delay diagnosis and/or adversely affect clinical management. The limited tissue obtained by CNB may hinder lesional architectural assessment and comprehensive ancillary testing, particularly when tissue is rapidly exhausted. In contrast, SEB generally provides more tissue for diagnostic evaluation, also favoring biobanking for future diagnostic and therapeutic needs and research purposes. We believe that SEB remains the preferred approach for accurate lymphoma characterization and subtyping when feasible. SEB and CNB should be considered complementary rather than mutually exclusive approaches, with CNB particularly useful in patients at increased surgical risk or presenting with deep-seated, surgically inaccessible lesions. When CNB results are inconclusive or discordant with clinical findings, repeat sampling, preferably by SEB whenever possible, should be recommended to establish a reliable diagnosis. Regardless of the sampling approach, careful tissue handling and appropriate pre-analytical procedures remain essential to ensure both the quality and the sustainability of the histopathological diagnostic process.

43050693.title: Nodal peripheral T-cell lymphoma: a prognostic index developed by the T-cell project.
43050693.author: Luminari S
43050693.abstract: To characterize real-world treatment patterns and outcomes in nodal peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL) and to develop and externally validate a contemporary clinical prognostic model, we analyzed patients prospectively registered in the International T-Cell Project 2 (TCP2). Between January 2018 and January 2026, 1,465 patients with PTCL were registered; 959 with nodal PTCL by the 2016 WHO classification (PTCL not otherwise specified (PTCL-NOS), systemic anaplastic large-cell lymphoma (ALCL; ALK-positive or ALK-negative), and T-follicular helper lymphoma (TFHL)) were analyzed. The primary endpoint was 2-year progression-free survival (PFS); the model was externally validated in the TCP1 cohort (n = 1,016). The cohort comprised 396 PTCL-NOS (41%), 263 TFHL (27%), 211 ALK-negative ALCL (22%), and 89 ALK-positive ALCL (9%). First-line therapy was CHOEP in 340 (37%), CHOP in 260 (29%), and brentuximab vedotin-CHP in 139 (15%); 156 underwent consolidative stem cell transplantation. After a median follow-up of 25.3 months, 2-year PFS and overall survival were 35.3% and 54.3%, respectively. In multivariate analysis, diagnosis other than ALCL, age ≥65 years, ECOG performance status ≥2, thrombocytopenia, extranodal involvement, and elevated LDH were independently associated with inferior PFS. A six-variable score using these factors stratified patients into 3 risk groups - low (score 0-1), intermediate (2-3), and high (4-6) with 2-year PFS, 65%, 33%, and 16% respectively (P < .001) and was confirmed in the TCP1 validation cohort. Outcomes for nodal PTCL remain poor with current therapy; the externally validated TCP score offers a contemporary, complementary tool for risk stratification and identification of patients at high risk of treatment failure. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03964480, NCT01142674.

43050692.title: Impact of Age on Real-World Outcomes of Bispecific Antibodies in Patients with Relapsed Refractory DLBCL: CUBIC Consortium Analysis.
43050692.author: Kambhampati Thiruvengadam S
43050692.abstract: Older patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) have limited treatment options. Bispecific antibodies (BsAbs) are a novel immunotherapy with less acute toxicity compared to conventional therapies. This is a real-world analysis conducted to understand the safety and efficacy of BsAbs in older compared to younger patients. Adult patients with relapsed/refractory DLBCL who received commercially available BsAbs as a single agent between June 2023 and October 2025 across 10 U.S. centers in the CUBIC consortium were included. Key efficacy outcomes included response rates and survival; safety outcomes included cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS). The analysis included 256 patients stratified by 3 age groups: <65 (71 patients), 65-74 (81 patients), ≥75 (104 patients). Median prior lines of therapy was 3, 80% were refractory to most recent therapy, and 40% would have been considered pivotal trial ineligible. At median follow-up of 9 months, the 12-month progression-free survival (PFS) was 30% and 12-month overall survival (OS) was 45%. Grade ≥3 CRS occurred in 5% patients; ICANS grade ≥3 occurred in 2% patients. There was no statistically significant difference in outcomes between the 3 age cohorts <65, 65-74, ≥75 with 12-month PFS 21%, 26%, 38%; 12-month OS 35%, 42%, 49%; grade ≥3 CRS 6%, 5%, 4%; and grade ≥3 ICANS 3%, 2%, 1% respectively. On multivariable analysis, ECOG ≥2 and elevated LDH were associated with inferior PFS and OS. Our analysis demonstrates that BsAbs maintain comparable efficacy and safety across all age groups, including patients ≥75 years.

43039893.title: Lenalidomide and rituximab for relapsed/refractory follicular lymphoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
43039893.author: Matarasso Greenfeld S
43039893.abstract: Lenalidomide (len) and rituximab (R2) is standard second-line therapy for follicular lymphoma (FL), and the backbone and comparator for several new therapies. This systematic review and meta-analysis of R2 or len-anti-CD20 monoclonal antibodies aims to clarify efficacy across trials, and to evaluate the benefit of triplet therapies including R2. Across 24 treatment arms involving 2245 patients, 63% received R2 or len-anti-CD20 and 37% received it with an additional agent. For R2/len-anti-CD20, the overall response rate (ORR) was 75.9% (95% CI 72.1-79.3, p = 0.0092; I2 = 53.5%), and complete response rates (CR), 39.6% (95% CI 32.4-47.3, p < 0.0001, I2 = 73.2%). ORRs were similar whether studies included or excluded rituximab-refractory, but CR appeared lower (28.6% vs. 42.9%). The number of prior lines of therapy did not affect response. Adding a third agent to R2 or len-anti-CD20 resulted in similar ORRs but significantly higher CR and 1- and 2-year progression-free survival appeared longer than that seen with R2. However, triplet regimens were associated with increased grade ≥3 toxicity. These findings reinforce the role of R2 in R/R FL in the modern treatment era. R2 at first relapse is effective across rituximab sensitivity profiles. Triplet combinations built on the R2 backbone improve efficacy but require careful patient selection and monitoring due to higher toxicity risks.

43053209.title: Chemotherapy-induced mast-cell degranulation constrains tertiary lymphoid maturation in lung cancer brain metastasis.
43053209.author: Fu M
43053209.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) support local adaptive immunity and are associated with favorable antitumor responses across multiple cancers. However, how anticancer treatment reshapes TLS maturation, particularly in lung cancer brain metastasis (LCBM), remains poorly understood.
METHODS: We integrated clinicopathological profiling of LCBM cohorts with bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial profiling, immune-repertoire analysis, histological validation, and murine intracranial tumor models. Associations between prior treatment and TLS maturation were evaluated using multivariable analyses. Mechanistic studies examined chemotherapy-associated IL-33 release, mast-cell activation, and the effects of PGD2 on antigen-specific T-cell cytotoxicity and B-cell differentiation. Pharmacological inhibition of H-PGDS and mast-cell stabilization were further evaluated in vivo.
RESULTS: Mature TLSs were associated with favorable survival in patients with LCBM, whereas preoperative chemotherapy was independently associated with impaired TLS maturation after adjustment for measured clinical and treatment covariates. Consistent with this observation, chemotherapy-treated tumors exhibited increased IL-33 levels, mast-cell accumulation, and enhanced mast-cell degranulation, with spatial analyses placing activated mast cells within TLS-associated immune niches. Mechanistically, IL-33 activated ST2-expressing mast cells, induced NF-κB-associated transcriptional programs. Functionally, mast cell-derived PGD2 suppressed antigen-specific CD8⁺ T-cell cytotoxicity and impaired plasma-cell differentiation, providing a potential link between chemotherapy and weakened local adaptive immunity. In vivo, pharmacological inhibition of H-PGDS enhanced chemotherapy efficacy, while mast-cell stabilization with cromolyn sodium reduced chemotherapy-associated degranulation, increased local adaptive immune-cell infiltration, improved intracranial tumor control, and prolonged survival when combined with chemotherapy.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings support a model in which chemotherapy-associated tissue stress activates an IL-33-responsive mast-cell program and restrains TLS-associated adaptive immunity in LCBM. Although this pathway is unlikely to operate as an exclusively linear or mast-cell-specific mechanism, targeting mast-cell-associated inflammatory signaling may provide a strategy to preserve antitumor immunity and improve the therapeutic efficacy of chemotherapy in brain metastasis.

43053183.title: Dual-targeting BCMA/CD19 CAR T cells with asymmetric 4-1BB/CD28-YMFM costimulation in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma: a phase 1/2 trial with single-cell profiling of extramedullary disease.
43053183.author: Jiang H
43053183.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extramedullary disease (EMD) predicts poor outcomes after B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM). KQ-2003 is a bicistronic BCMA/CD19 CAR T-cell product incorporating 4-1BB and CD28-YMFM costimulatory domains. We assessed its activity and intralesional biology, focusing on EMD.
METHODS: Twenty-four patients received KQ-2003 (21 trial participants; three compassionate-use patients). Hematologic and EMD responses were assessed using International Myeloma Working Group (IMWG) and Italian Myeloma criteria for PET Use, respectively. Bone marrow minimal residual disease (MRD) was assessed by next-generation flow cytometry (10- 5 sensitivity). Progression-free survival (PFS) was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox methods. Longitudinal single-cell RNA sequencing profiled one patient's infusion product, serial blood, and spatially distinct EMD biopsies.
RESULTS: Patients had received a median of five prior lines; 18 (75.0%) were triple-class refractory, six (25.0%) penta-refractory, 23 (95.8%) had high-risk cytogenetics, and 15 (62.5%) had EMD. All 20 patients with measurable hematologic disease achieved hematologic responses (18 [90.0%] complete/stringent complete); IMWG-defined overall response rate was 95.0%. Fourteen (93.3%) of 15 EMD patients achieved metabolic responses (13 [86.7%] complete). Among 19 baseline MRD-positive patients, 12 (63.2%) became MRD-negative by month 6; 10 and six also had documented negativity at months 12 and 24, respectively. At 29.2 months' median follow-up, median PFS was 24.0 months (95% CI, 15.0-not reached); no significant difference was detected by baseline EMD status (HR, 0.92; P = 0.89). Among the 21 trial participants, grade ≥ 3 cytokine release syndrome and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome occurred in one (4.8%) and two (9.5%), respectively; two treatment-related fatal pneumonias occurred. Single-patient longitudinal profiling revealed proliferating lesion-infiltrating CAR T cells with increased CCL3/CCL4 expression and tumor-cell apoptotic and necroptotic transcriptional programs. Trajectory analysis suggested transcriptional links between tissue effectors and circulating CCL5-positive memory-like CAR T cells. CellChat predicted BCMA-related tumor-microenvironment interactions and immune-cell interactions involving circulating CAR T cells.
CONCLUSIONS: KQ-2003 produced deep, durable hematologic and metabolic responses in heavily pretreated, high-risk RRMM, including EMD. Intralesional profiling identified CAR T-cell proliferation, tumor-cell death-associated programs, and candidate microenvironmental interactions. These findings warrant further evaluation of this dual-targeting strategy in EMD.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04714827; registered 19 January 2021.
