43044123.title: Treatment journey and outcomes of patients with RRMM after quadruple-class exposure: a critical unmet need.
43044123.author: Hansen DK
43044123.abstract: Patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) previously exposed to proteasome inhibitors, immunomodulatory drugs, anti-CD38 monoclonal antibodies, and anti-B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) therapies, defined as quadruple-class exposed (QCEx), face poor prognoses and limited therapeutic options. This study retrospectively tracked treatment journeys of this population across lines of therapy (LOTs), documenting disease characteristics and clinical outcomes using deidentified electronic health record data from Flatiron Health database (January 2011-July 2025). In total, 21,112 patients with MM were identified; of these, 683 had QCEx RRMM, 241 initiated a subsequent (index) therapy, and 121 died before receiving an index therapy. At index, patients had a median 5 prior LOT (range, 1-14), 49.8% exhibiting quadruple-class refractory disease. The median age was 67 years (range, 37-85). The most common index regimens were G protein-coupled receptor class C group 5 D (GPRC5D) bispecific antibodies (17.8%), BCMA-targeted (11.6%), and chemotherapy-based (9.5%) regimens. Median event-free and overall survival were 5.0 months (95% CI, 4.0-5.8) and 15.6 months (95% CI, 12.2-22.0), respectively. Approximately 25% died before advancing to each additional LOT. These findings highlight the profound clinical unmet need among patients with QCEx RRMM. Early intervention with novel and effective therapies is crucial to improving outcomes.

43039361.title: An open agentic AI co-scientist for clinical and biomedical discovery.
43039361.author: Roberts KF
43039361.abstract: Biomedical research is constrained by the time and domain expertise required to analyze increasingly large and complex datasets. Here we present OpenScientist, an open-source agentic AI co-scientist designed to address this gap by investigating scientist-defined queries and generating verifiable, data-grounded analyses. OpenScientist was evaluated by domain experts across five biomedical case studies, completing analyses in minutes that otherwise would take months of human time and expertise. It accurately quantified Alzheimer's blood biomarker performance, generated a plasma proteomic survival model that predicted survival in a hidden-evaluation cohort, proposed a reproducible mechanism linking tau pathology to altered lysosomal acidification, generated multiple myeloma hypotheses validated in an external cohort with attenuated signal in randomized controls, and demonstrated concordance with an independent human analysis in a blinded, prespecified proteomic comparison. These results support the use of OpenScientist to assist biomedical data analysis in concert with human experts. To support research involving sensitive clinical datasets, OpenScientist can operate in a fully air-gapped environment using open-source models for inference. OpenScientist demonstrates that open, auditable, agentic AI can support real-world clinical research by researching the literature, generating hypotheses, executing analyses, and generating insights from complex datasets.

43038178.title: Carfilzomib-based strategies in transplant-eligible multiple myeloma: long-term follow-up of the phase 2 FORTE trial.
43038178.author: Bertuglia G
43038178.abstract: In the phase 2 FORTE trial, transplant-eligible newly diagnosed multiple myeloma patients aged ≤65 years were randomized to (R1) carfilzomib-lenalidomide-dexamethasone followed by autologous stem cell transplantation (KRd-ASCT), twelve cycles of KRd (KRd12), or carfilzomib-cyclophosphamide-dexamethasone followed by ASCT (KCd-ASCT). Eligible patients were then randomized (R2) to maintenance with carfilzomib for 2 years plus lenalidomide until progression (KR) or lenalidomide alone until progression (R). With extended follow-up (median 99 months from R1 and 85 months from R2), KRd-ASCT significantly increased progression-free survival (PFS, median 98 months) versus KRd12 (median 70 months; HR 0.71, p=0.027) and KCd-ASCT (median 67 months; HR 0.66, p=0.006). A significant benefit in PFS2 was also observed versus both KRd12 (HR 0.65, p=0.02) and KCd-ASCT (HR 0.68, p=0.04) and in terms of overall survival (OS) versus KCd-ASCT (8-year OS: 76% vs 68%; HR 0.65, p=0.04). KR maintenance significantly improved PFS versus R (HR 0.67, p=0.02), with a time-dependent effect persisting up to two years after carfilzomib discontinuation; no differences in PFS2/OS were observed. KR significantly increased rate of measurable residual disease (MRD) conversion (sHR 0.47, p=0.03) during active treatment, and reduced MRD resurgence (sHR 0.53, p=0.001) versus R. Median duration of MRD negativity was 50.5 months in KR vs. 38 months in R arm. MRD-negative patients had significantly prolonged PFS with KR (HR 0.60, p=0.031); MRD-positive patients benefited from KR mainly during carfilzomib therapy (HR 0.46, p=0.05). The cumulative incidence of second primary malignancies was 6%. In conclusion, long-term follow-up confirms the high effectiveness of KRd-ASCT and KR maintenance. NCT02203643.

43038173.title: Etentamig in Relapsed/Refractory Multiple Myeloma: Pooled Phase 1 Data of an Investigational BCMA Bispecific Antibody.
43038173.author: Baljevic M
43038173.abstract: Etentamig is an investigational B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) x CD3 bispecific T-cell engager, composed of a low-affinity CD3 binding domain, potentially reducing cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and infections, a high-avidity bivalent BCMA-binding domain, and retained FcRn binding supporting monthly (Q4W) dosing after a single step-up dose (SUD). We report long-term efficacy and safety from the ongoing, open-label, phase 1 (dose escalation/expansion; NCT03933735) and Arm A of the phase 1b (NCT05650632) studies of etentamig in adult patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, triple-class exposure, and ≥3 prior lines of therapy (LoT). In phase 1, patients received etentamig 60 mg Q4W or 40 mg Q3W, and in phase 1b, a SUD on Day 1 and 60 mg Q4W on Day 4. Among 146 patients (median age: 68 years; median [range] prior LoT: 4 [3-23]), median follow-up was 13 months (range: 1-48). Objective responses and ≥ very good partial responses occurred in 66% and 54% of patients. Median duration of response and progression-free survival were not reached. Pooled data suggest etentamig has a manageable safety profile, with Grade 3/4 neutropenia and infection occurring in 38% and 23% of patients. In phase 1b Arm A (n=23), overall CRS incidence was 30% (26% Grade 1; 4% Grade 2) with modified dexamethasone premedication and 1 SUD; median onset was 22.3 hours (range: 5.5-29.6) hours, with resolution in 20.7 hours (range: 1.8-131.7). Etentamig's molecular design may be associated with the observed clinical efficacy and tolerability while also potentially supporting extended dosing intervals.

43035762.title: Successful treatment of systemic light chain amyloidosis with a novel high-avidity BCMA CAR.
43035762.author: Farid KMN
43035762.abstract: B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) is a promising target for immunotherapy in plasma cell dyscrasias, but no commercial BCMA-directed CAR T-cell product is approved in Europe for patients with systemic light chain (AL) amyloidosis. We used the in-house manufactured 2nd-generation BCMA-directed MDC-CAR-BCMA001 for the treatment of patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) AL amyloidosis. This is the first experience with this new high-avidity, academic CAR T-cell product in this population. Seven patients received 800 × 106 CAR T-cells after lymphodepletion. Leukapheresis, manufacturing and administration of CAR T-cells were performed in-house. Six patients had triple-class refractory disease (5/7 (71%) with prior high-dose chemotherapy). Active disease was present in 6/7 (86%) patients prior to CAR T-cell infusion. Overall response was observed in 6/7 patients (ORR 86%, 3 MRD-negative complete remissions). All patients with durable hematologic responses showed organ responses (cardiac, renal, improvement in polyneuropathy and myopathy) with rapid suppression of amyloidogenic free light chains. Six patients (86%) are alive, and 3/6 responders remain in remission after a median follow-up of 10.9 months. All patients experienced cytokine release syndrome, 5/7 grade ≤ 2, two grade 3, resolving after tocilizumab and/or dexamethasone. One patient experienced low-grade late immune effector cell-associated hematotoxicity. No neurotoxicity was observed. MDC-CAR-BCMA001 demonstrates high efficacy with manageable toxicity, making it a promising treatment for AL amyloidosis patients with preexisting organ insufficiencies. Deep responses and MRD negativity enable meaningful organ responses. Further evaluation as second-line therapy is planned in the ongoing clinical trial designated CLEAR AL (EU CT No. 2025-520790-39-00).

43052243.title: Immune effector cell associated hematotoxicity (ICAHT) with BCMA CAR T cell therapy in the earlier lines.
43052243.author: Mohan M
43052243.abstract: B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy is highly effective in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (MM), but adverse effects such as immune effector cell-associated hematotoxicity (ICAHT) remain a challenging early and long-term toxicity. Most reports on ICAHT originate from CAR T-cell therapies in late-stage MM, with limited data from earlier-line treatment. We conducted a multi-institutional retrospective study of 245 MM patients treated with BCMA CAR T, comparing ICAHT between early-line [early CAR T] (1-3 prior lines; n = 69) and late-line [late CAR T] (≥4 prior lines; n = 176) cohorts. Cytopenias (neutropenia ≤1000/µL, thrombocytopenia ≤50,000/µL, anemia ≤9 g/dL) were assessed at day 21 (D + 21), 3, and 6 months post-CAR T-cell infusion. At D + 21, ICAHT was less frequent with early CAR T versus late CAR T (39% vs 62%; p = 0.002), driven largely by lower thrombocytopenia (17% vs 39%; p = 0.001). At 3 months, ICAHT remained more common with late CAR T (30% vs 12%; p = 0.004), but by 6 months, rates converged (8.9% vs 18%; p = 0.126). Blood counts among patients with ICAHT at D + 21 often remained inferior at 3 and 6 months despite stem cell boosts. ICAHT at D + 21 independently predicted worse overall survival (HR 3.12; p = 0.022). Early-line CAR T-cell therapy was associated with superior 12-month PFS (87.8% vs 65.4%) and OS (96.2% vs 85.9%). These real-world data show that ICAHT occurs even with earlier-line BCMA CAR T-cell therapy, though less severe, and underscore the prognostic importance of early post-infusion cytopenias.

43064238.title: Artificial Intelligence in Thoracic Pathology and Biomarker Assessment: An IASLC Pathology Committee Review.
43064238.author: Le Quesne J
43064238.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is starting to transform pathology by enhancing diagnostic accuracy, prognostication, and therapeutic prediction through advanced computational analysis of histopathological images. This review explores key AI methodologies and their applications in lung cancer diagnostics. Supervised learning dominates current clinical AI tools, relying on annotated whole-slide images (WSIs) for tasks like tumor subtyping, quantitation of tissue-based parameters, prediction of driver alterations (e.g. EGFR and KRAS mutations, ALK rearrangement), and assessment of tumor microenvironment (TME) features. Meanwhile, weakly supervised and self-supervised learning (SSL) methods, such as multiple instance learning (MIL) and contrastive learning, reduce dependency on labor-intensive annotations and uncover novel prognostic morphologic patterns. AI demonstrates strong performance in predicting therapeutic responses, including immune checkpoint inhibitor efficacy and pathologic response to neoadjuvant therapy, while emerging techniques like spatial transcriptomics and multiplex immunofluorescence further leverage AI to decode complex spatial biology and generate novel biomarkers. Despite much progress, major challenges persist in validation, reliability, interpretability, regulatory approval, ethics and data privacy standards, cost and reimbursement, equity, and integration into clinical workflows. Adoption requires scalable digital pathology infrastructure, interdisciplinary collaboration, and suitable reimbursement frameworks. Regulatory efforts aim to address ethical and safety concerns, but global harmonization remains incomplete. We also consider the professional consequences of adoption, including cognitive deskilling, workforce displacement, and the conditions under which pathologist oversight remains meaningful rather than nominal, and argue that liability should follow the reality of control. As AI evolves, particularly with foundation models and large language models (LLMs), thoracic pathology stands to benefit from substantially extended diagnostic and predictive capabilities, pending resolution of implementation barriers.

43064237.title: IASLC Multidisciplinary Recommendations for Assessment and Reporting of Lymph Node Treatment Response in Lung Cancer Resection Specimens After Neoadjuvant Therapy.
43064237.author: Berezowska S
43064237.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pathologic response (PR) after neoadjuvant therapy is an established surrogate endpoint in lung cancer clinical trials. Although IASLC recommendations standardizing PR assessment in primary tumors are widely adopted, guidance for evaluating treatment response in regional lymph nodes (LNs) has been lacking. The IASLC has developed multidisciplinary consensus recommendations for LN assessment in resected lung cancer specimens following neoadjuvant therapy.
METHODS: A core group of IASLC pathologists drafted statements addressing key aspects of gross and microscopic LN evaluation. These were refined through a two-round Delphi process involving 48 international experts in thoracic oncology, surgery, radiology, and pathology. Consensus was predefined as ≥85% agreement. Experts reviewed, commented upon, and voted on 13 final recommendations.
RESULTS: All 13 recommendations reached consensus (86-100%). Key statements include: defining pathologic complete response (pCR) as the absence of residual viable tumor (RVT) in both lung and LNs; introducing MPR(N+) for cases with ≤10% RVT at the primary site but residual nodal disease; requiring estimation of RVT, stroma, and necrosis across LN stations; accepting unweighted ("eyeball") microscopic assessment; encouraging reporting of metastasis size; and advising complete LN submission with selective use of deeper levels and/or immunohistochemistry. The recommendations further clarify interpretation of direct tumor extension into LN, interpretation of psammoma bodies or acellular mucin, and interactions with ypTNM staging principles.
CONCLUSION: These IASLC multidisciplinary recommendations provide the first standardized framework for assessing treatment response in LNs after neoadjuvant therapy in lung cancer and are intended to improve diagnostic reproducibility, support trial harmonization, and to outline research opportunities.

43064236.title: Global Practices in the Diagnosis and Management of Thymic Epithelial Tumors: An International Thymic Malignancy Interest Group Survey and Multidisciplinary Discussion.
43064236.author: Roden AC
43064236.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) are rare malignancies. Since they occur infrequently, most physicians encounter only a small number of patients, resulting in limited experience with their diagnosis and management and a scarcity of large-scale studies. Nevertheless, TNM staging was developed for all TETs in 2017, and guidelines for diagnosis and management of these tumors, largely based on expert opinion, are available.
OBJECTIVE: To better understand the utilization of the TNM staging system by providers, and their awareness and knowledge of current recommendations for the diagnosis and management of patients with TET.
METHOD: A global survey of medical oncologists, pathologists, radiation oncologists, radiologists, and thoracic surgeons was conducted.
RESULTS: Based on 398 contributors, we found many areas of agreement among physicians but also areas of controversy. For instance, the acceptance of TNM staging was over 90%, but some providers still solely used the Masaoka-Koga staging system. Other agreements and controversies were identified and reported in this paper. To our knowledge, this is the largest international multidisciplinary survey on diagnosis and management of TET.
CONCLUSIONS: Our results confirmed that continuous education about the latest literature and available recommendations, guidelines, and TNM staging is important, and ongoing, ideally multi-institutional, global research is imperative, with the goal of developing a standardized, evidence-based approach to the diagnosis and management of patients with TETs.

43063366.title: Survival Outcomes of Sequential Therapies in Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma: A Real-World Analysis of Second-Line Treatment With Nivolumab or Carboplatin-Pemetrexed.
43063366.author: Maffezzoli M
43063366.abstract:
PURPOSE: Optimal treatment sequencing in malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM) remains uncertain, particularly after progression on first-line (1L) treatment. We assessed real-world outcomes of patients receiving second-line (2L) carboplatin-pemetrexed (CARBO-PEM) after nivolumab-ipilimumab (NIVO-IPI), or 2L nivolumab (NIVO) after CARBO-PEM and explored the prognostic value of the Mesothelioma Risk Score (MRS) in the 1L setting.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included patients with advanced MPM treated across five UK institutions between May 2015 and November 2025. Eligible patients received either 2L CARBO-PEM after NIVO-IPI, or 1L CARBO-PEM followed by 2L NIVO. The primary end point was overall survival (OS) from 1L treatment initiation.
RESULTS: Overall, 147 patients were included, and 54 received NIVO-IPI followed by CARBO-PEM and 93 received CARBO-PEM followed by NIVO. The median age was 73.8 years and 83.0% had epithelioid histology. The median follow-up was 43.3 months from 1L initiation. The median OS was 23.55 months with CARBO-PEM followed by NIVO versus 25.53 months with NIVO-IPI followed by CARBO-PEM (hazard ratio 1.28 [95% CI, 0.82 to 2.01]; P = .270). The median PFS 2L was 3.65 months with 2L NIVO versus 6.15 months with 2L CARBO-PEM, without statistical significance, while median OS 2L was 12.53 months and 14.11, respectively. In the 1L setting, MRS showed limited discrimination for PFS and OS. Grade ≥2 irAEs during NIVO-IPI were associated with longer PFS 1L but not OS.
CONCLUSION: In patients with MPM receiving 2L therapy, CARBO-PEM after NIVO-IPI remains clinically active, and OS appeared similar across treatment sequences. These findings support sequence flexibility in fit patients but highlight the need for more robust prognostic biomarkers.

43057628.title: Nivolumab Plus Ipilimumab as First-Line Treatment for Patients With Metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Final, 7.5-Year Outcomes From CheckMate 227.
43057628.author: Reck M
43057628.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The phase 3 CheckMate 227 Part 1 study (NCT02477826) demonstrated survival benefit with first-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab versus chemotherapy in patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Here, we report final, 7.5-year efficacy and safety results.
METHODS: Adults with stage IV/recurrent NSCLC and no sensitizing EGFR/ALK mutations were stratified by programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) ≥1% (n = 1189) or <1% (n = 550) and randomized to nivolumab plus ipilimumab, nivolumab alone (PD-L1 ≥1% only), nivolumab plus chemotherapy (PD-L1 <1% only), or chemotherapy alone. Assessments included overall survival (OS), duration of response, and safety.
RESULTS: At a minimum follow-up of 91.9 months, nivolumab plus ipilimumab continued to demonstrate long-term OS benefit versus chemotherapy in patients with tumor PD-L1 ≥1% (7-year OS rates, 19% versus 10%; hazard ratio [HR], 0.78; 95% CI: 0.67-0.91) or tumor PD-L1 <1% (7-year OS rates, 14% versus 4%; HR, 0.64; 95% CI: 0.51-0.79). Rates of ongoing response at 7 years were higher with nivolumab plus ipilimumab than chemotherapy among responders with tumor PD-L1 ≥1% (25% versus 3%) or tumor PD-L1 <1% (20% versus 3%). Clinical benefit with nivolumab plus ipilimumab was observed across most patient subgroups, including those with squamous or non-squamous NSCLC or selected oncogenic driver mutations. No new safety signals were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: This final analysis from CheckMate 227 confirms that nivolumab plus ipilimumab confers long-term, durable clinical benefit versus chemotherapy in patients with metastatic NSCLC across both the tumor PD-L1 ≥1% and PD-L1 <1% populations, reinforcing nivolumab plus ipilimumab as a first-line treatment option for these patients.

43056109.title: Computed Tomography Screening and Small Cell Lung Cancer Stage Shift and Survival.
43056109.author: Potter AL
43056109.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Lung cancer screening with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) has been shown to identify lung cancers at earlier stages and to significantly reduce lung cancer mortality in prior randomized clinical trials. However, the benefit of LDCT screening for small cell lung cancer (SCLC), an aggressive subtype of lung cancer, is unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the characteristics and outcomes of SCLC diagnosed after a lung cancer screening examination using a large database of Medicare beneficiaries.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this retrospective cohort study, Medicare data linked to the Surveillance Epidemiology End Results Program's cancer registry data were analyzed. Patients in the US aged 65 to 78 years who were diagnosed with SCLC from 2015 to 2021 were identified for analysis, with follow-up data through 2022. Patients who underwent 1 or more LDCT lung cancer screening examinations during the 12 months preceding their SCLC diagnosis were included in the screened group. All other patients were included in the unscreened group. Data were analyzed from January to August 2026.
EXPOSURE: One or more LDCT lung cancer screenings during the 12 months preceding SCLC diagnosis.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcomes were stage at SCLC diagnosis and overall survival after SCLC diagnosis in the screened and unscreened groups.
RESULTS: A total of 17 099 patients (median [IQR] age, 72.0 [69.0-75.0] years; 8999 [52.6%] female) met study inclusion criteria, of which 949 (5.5%) were included in the screened group and 16 150 (94.5%) were included in the unscreened group. When compared with patients in the unscreened group, patients in the screened group were significantly less likely to be diagnosed with distant disease (419 of 949 [44.2%] vs 11 376 of 16 150 [70.4%]; P < .001). Patients in the screened group also had significantly better overall survival when compared with patients in the unscreened group (3-year overall survival, 28.0% [95% CI, 24.9%-31.2%] vs 10.8% [95% CI, 10.3%-11.3%]; P < .001). Both findings were consistent in propensity score-matched analysis.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this cohort study of Medicare beneficiaries diagnosed with SCLC suggest that receipt of lung cancer screening was associated with a shift toward earlier-stage SCLC at diagnosis and improved overall survival.

43063810.title: Systemic therapy and radiotherapy for small-cell lung cancer brain metastases.
43063810.author: Luo X
43063810.abstract: Brain metastases are a defining biological feature of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) and a persistent blind spot in therapeutic development. Chemo-immunotherapy has improved survival in extensive-stage SCLC, and durvalumab consolidation has changed care for limited-stage disease, but these advances do not establish intracranial efficacy. Patients with active or symptomatic brain metastases remain under-represented in pivotal trials; brain imaging is inconsistent; and prophylactic cranial irradiation, previous radiotherapy and corticosteroid exposure confound interpretation. Emerging DLL3-directed T-cell engagers and B7-H3-directed antibody-drug conjugates have nevertheless generated prospective intracranial activity signals. This narrative review integrates CNS assessment, radiotherapy and prevention, systemic treatment, treatment sequencing, leptomeningeal disease and the biological and methodological questions that determine clinical interpretation. Radiotherapy selection requires lesion size and volume, neurological status, prior treatment and reliable MRI surveillance; emerging systemic activity does not establish that local therapy or prophylactic cranial irradiation can routinely be omitted. We distinguish systemic efficacy in populations that include brain metastases from demonstrated intracranial activity and propose a CNS-specific evidence hierarchy. Future trials should mandate brain MRI, separate treated-stable from untreated-asymptomatic disease, use RANO-BM-compatible endpoints, report corticosteroid and radiotherapy exposure, and incorporate paired plasma and cerebrospinal-fluid analyses.

43067256.title: Clinicogenomic landscape of small cell carcinoma and identification of potentially actionable genomic alterations by comprehensive genomic profiling.
43067256.author: Kunimatsu Y
43067256.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Small cell carcinoma (SCC) is an aggressive malignancy that commonly arises in the lung and can develop in extrapulmonary organs. Although organ-specific genomic studies have been reported, the clinicogenomic landscape of SCC across primary sites remains poorly characterized. We conducted a nationwide Japanese clinicogenomic analysis to characterize recurrent and organ-specific molecular features and assess their potential therapeutic actionability in SCC.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We obtained clinicogenomic data from the Center for Cancer Genomics and Advanced Therapeutics (C-CAT) database, and included patients with SCC who underwent comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) between June 2019 and February 2025. Genomic alterations were annotated using OncoKB therapeutic evidence levels, and each patient was assigned to the highest level identified.
RESULTS: Among 95,234 patients who underwent CGP, 615 (0.65%) had SCC, including 320 with small cell lung cancer (SCLC) and 295 with extrapulmonary SCC (EPSCC). TP53 (73.0%) and RB1 (49.9%) alterations were the most frequent events. Organ-specific genomic features included frequent TERT alterations in bladder SCC, PTEN alterations in prostate SCC, and SMARCA4 alterations in ovarian SCC. Furthermore, EGFR alterations were significantly associated with never-smoking status in SCLC after multiple-testing correction and adjustment for age and sex. CGP identified potentially actionable alterations corresponding to OncoKB Levels 1, 2, 3A, or 3B in 12.2% of patients, including ERBB2 amplification in 3.7%.
CONCLUSIONS: SCC demonstrates recurrent genomic alterations and substantial organ-specific molecular heterogeneity across primary sites. CGP identified potentially actionable genomic alterations in a subset of patients, while the clinical relevance of these findings requires further evaluation.

43067216.title: HER2 status in Diffuse pleural mesothelioma.
43067216.author: Ragazzi M
43067216.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diffuse pleural mesothelioma (DPM) is an aggressive, most commonly asbestos-related malignancy with limited therapeutic options. HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugates active against HER2-low tumors have renewed interest in HER2 assessment across malignancies, yet no DPM-specific HER2 scoring system exists and the impact of applying tumor-specific guidelines to DPM is unknown.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We evaluated HER2 expression by immunohistochemistry, with FISH confirmation, in 53 consecutive DPM patients, and compared classification when the breast, gastric, and colorectal scoring guidelines were applied in parallel to the same cases.
RESULTS: HER2 membrane staining was detected in 9 cases (17.0%), consistently faint-barely perceptible, incomplete, and segmental (median 5% of neoplastic cells), with no overexpression or amplification. The identical staining pattern yielded markedly discordant scores: most cases were classified as "0″ under breast criteria but as "1+" under gastric and colorectal criteria. HER2 expression was confined to epithelioid components.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings show that, in the absence of a validated DPM-specific scoring system, HER2 guidelines are not interchangeable, a methodological caveat with direct implications for biomarker comparability and for interpreting "HER2-low" status in the era of next-generation antibody - drug conjugates.

43056990.title: Navitoclax overcomes epithelial-mesenchymal transition-associated resistance in ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer with rapid disease progression during alectinib treatment.
43056990.author: Nishimura T
43056990.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) generally responds to the ALK tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) alectinib; however, some patients experience rapid disease progression shortly after treatment initiation. This study investigated the molecular features underlying this clinically distinct phenotype and evaluated potential therapeutic strategies using patient-derived models.
METHODS: A 68-year-old woman with ALK-positive NSCLC experienced disease progression within 1 month of first-line alectinib therapy despite an initial transient tumor response. Two resistant cell lines were established from an adrenal metastasis and a pleural effusion, respectively. Histopathological and molecular characterization was performed. The combination of ALK-TKIs and the B-cell lymphoma 2 family inhibitor navitoclax was evaluated in vitro and in vivo.
RESULTS: Both cell lines harbored the EML4-ALK fusion variant 1 without secondary ALK mutations and demonstrated resistance to multiple ALK-TKIs. Transcriptomic profiling demonstrated epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-associated features in the resistant cell lines, supported by concordant immunohistochemical findings in the pretreatment specimen. Melanoma-associated antigen 3 (MAGE-A3) was identified as the most highly upregulated gene, and its knockdown significantly enhanced ALK-TKI sensitivity. Navitoclax combined with ALK-TKIs synergistically reduced cell viability and enhanced apoptosis in vitro, and lorlatinib plus navitoclax produced greater antitumor efficacy than either monotherapy in vivo.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that pre-existing EMT-associated features, together with MAGE-A3 upregulation and impaired apoptotic signaling, may contribute to rapid disease progression during alectinib treatment in a subset of ALK-positive NSCLC patients. Targeting apoptotic vulnerability with navitoclax in combination with ALK-TKIs warrants further investigation as a therapeutic strategy for this resistance phenotype.

43056991.title: Bridging the molecular and immune landscapes of pleural mesothelioma: Implications for immune checkpoint inhibitor response.
43056991.author: Soares-Gonçalves J
43056991.abstract: Pleural mesothelioma is a rare, asbestos-related malignancy with limited therapeutic options and dismal survival. Despite regulatory efforts, ongoing exposures, long disease latency and cases without recognized exposure suggest that pleural mesothelioma will remain a global challenge for decades. Immune checkpoint inhibitors yield modest, although clinically meaningful benefit in a subset of patients, and histology alone incompletely captures the pronounced intra- and inter-patient heterogeneity that drives prognosis and treatment responses. Multi-omic studies depict pleural mesothelioma as a tumor suppressor loss malignancy with low mutation rates, extensive structural genomic damage and a spectrum of immune states. In this review, we bridge genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic and immune-profiling data to explain how asbestos-induced genomic fragility, germline predisposition and the tumor immune microenvironment interact to shape disease biology and therapeutic vulnerability. We highlight how histo-molecular and immune-vascular continua refine risk stratification beyond histology, and how recurrent alterations intersect with immune infiltration, checkpoint expression and T cell dysfunction to potentially modulate immune checkpoint inhibitors sensitivity. These insights support comprehensive and integrative profiling to develop robust biomarkers, optimize patient selection and guide rational combinatorial strategies.

43062205.title: Telemedicine Follow-Up During Intensive Pediatric Cancer Treatment: Patient- and Family-Reported Outcomes, Secondary Analysis of the KULT-SH Trial.
43062205.author: Exner B
43062205.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children undergoing high-intensity cancer therapy require frequent follow-up visits due to the high risk of complications, which can place a substantial burden on patients and their families. Although telemedicine may reduce this burden, evidence on its use during the high-intensity treatment phase in pediatric oncology is currently lacking.
METHODS: This analysis is based on the KULT-SH crossover trial conducted in Northern Germany. A total of 55 children and young adults aged 1-25 years undergoing intensive oncological treatment were randomized to receive telemedicine or in-person outpatient visits for 3 months each, with telemedicine applied to selected follow-up visits. Health-related quality of life (HRQoL) was assessed during the high-intensity treatment phase using the KINDL-R questionnaire. Additional questionnaires evaluated organizational burden and caregiver- and patient-reported experiences with telemedicine and in-person care, and satisfaction with care.
RESULTS: No statistically significant difference in longitudinal overall HRQoL was detected between telemedicine and in-person phases. Exploratory analyses in children aged 1-6 years suggested higher HRQoL during the telemedicine phase in selected domains. Caregivers reported significantly reduced organizational burden during telemedicine, including less work absence, reduced need for sibling care, and shorter waiting times. Both patients and caregivers reported more available time during telemedicine across all domains. Exploratory retrospective assessments suggested better patient-reported well-being during telemedicine, whereas satisfaction with care was comparable between study phases.
CONCLUSION: These findings support telemedicine as a feasible complement to conventional care during the high-intensity treatment phase in pediatric oncology, with reduced logistical burden and no detected adverse difference in longitudinal HRQoL or satisfaction with care.

43062204.title: From Data to Duty: An Informatics Blueprint for Pediatric Oncology Trials.
43062204.author: Wyatt KD
43062204.abstract: The data generated by cooperative-group clinical trials have transformed outcomes for children with cancer, yet the infrastructure underlying their collection and use has not kept pace with advances in informatics and data science. Data collection on pediatric oncology trials remains largely manual: Clinical research assistants abstract values from medical records and key them into electronic case report forms, a process that is costly, slow, inconsistent, and error-prone. Data are often siloed within trial networks for years after a study closes, limiting their value for secondary research, particularly for rare cancers. In this consensus blueprint, an interdisciplinary group of pediatric oncologists, clinical informaticians, data scientists, nurses, clinical research assistants, drug developers, and parent advocates outlines a pragmatic path forward across three components of the data lifecycle: collection, processing, and sharing. We argue that case report forms should be bound to standardized common data elements; that automated data abstraction from electronic health records, including via large language models with human-in-the-loop validation, should replace much of today's manual abstraction; that paper chemotherapy roadmaps should be reconceived as computable artifacts; and that clinical trials data should be deposited in publicly accessible repositories with appropriate governance as soon as practically feasible. We discuss facilitators and barriers within each component, including standards adoption, regulatory complexity, financial sustainability, and workforce capacity. We propose concrete actions for funders, clinical trials networks, professional societies, and industry. The technology to achieve these goals exists today, and widespread adoption requires coordinated leadership, sustainable funding models, and a cultural shift that recognizes data stewardship as an ethical imperative and a duty to the children and families we serve.

43062201.title: Local Treatment for Perineal and Perianal Rhabdomyosarcoma: Clinical Practice Guidelines and Consensus Statement From the Children's Oncology Group, European Pediatric Soft Tissue Sarcoma Study Group, the Cooperative Weichteilsarkom Studiengruppe, and the International Soft Tissue Sarcoma Consortium.
43062201.author: Seitz G
43062201.abstract: Local control of rhabdomyosarcoma in the perianal and perineal region (PRMS) is challenging due to the unfavorable tumor location, the often advanced stage of disease, the prevalence of alveolar histology with PAX3/FOXO1 fusion, and frequent regional lymph node (LN) involvement at presentation. Distant metastases are present at diagnosis in up to 49% of patients. Given the high risk of recurrence, the prognosis of patients with PRMS treated with multimodal treatment is poor, with a reported 5-year overall survival (OS) rate of 39%-52%. Due to the rarity of PRMS along with variations in treatment protocols over time and across different cooperative groups, we have developed consensus local treatment guidelines. This guideline is based on a comprehensive literature review and expert opinion and is endorsed by the International Soft-Tissue Sarcoma Consortium (INSTRuCT). It integrates insights from three leading pediatric oncology cooperative groups: the Cooperative Weichteilsarkom Studiengruppe (CWS; since December 2024 part of European pediatric Soft-tissue sarcoma Study Group [EpSSG]), Children's Oncology Group (COG), and EpSSG. This document addresses surgical therapy options, including biopsy, nodal staging, and various resection modalities, as well as options for radiotherapy, such as intensity-modulated radiation therapy, proton beam therapy, and brachytherapy.

43062150.title: Indocyanine Green Assists in Identification of Solid Tumor Pulmonary Metastases.
43062150.author: Carter M
43062150.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The presence of pulmonary metastases reduces overall survival in patients with certain solid tumors; therefore, surgical clearance is crucial to cure for some types. This multi-institutional prospective study sought to determine the utility and diagnostic accuracy of indocyanine green (ICG) for delineating pulmonary metastases in diverse pediatric, adolescent, and young adult solid cancers.
PROCEDURE: Thirteen member institutions of the Pediatric Surgical Oncology Research Collaborative administered preoperative ICG to patients undergoing pulmonary metastasectomy for primary or recurrent solid tumor malignancy (2019-2023). Surgeons reported their perspective on ICG utility for pulmonary metastasectomy following each operation. The diagnostic accuracy of ICG fluorescence to identify a pathologically confirmed tumor-containing specimen was determined.
RESULTS: Of 829 specimens resected during 134 pulmonary metastasectomies (30.6% hepatic, 47.0% osteosarcoma, 17.2% non-osteosarcoma-type sarcomas ["other sarcomas"], 5.2% other non-hepatic and non-sarcoma tumor types ["other tumor types"]). Surgeons reported ICG as helpful in 77.6% of procedures. In 11.9% of cases, ICG identified viable metastases not visualized on preoperative imaging. Adjusted diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity (95% confidence interval [CI]) for metastases from all tumor types was 80.7% (77.9%-83.3%) and 82.5% (78.9%-85.8%), respectively. By primary tumor histology, adjusted accuracy and sensitivity (95% CI) were 83.2% (74.4%-89.9%), 46.7% (28.3%-65.7%) for metastases from other sarcomas, 80.6% (75.3%-85.2%), 95.6% (91.8%-98.0%) for hepatic tumors, 80.6% (76.6%-84.2%), 77.1% (71.4%-82.2%) for osteosarcoma, and 72.7% (49.8%-89.3%), 60.0% (26.2%-87.8%) for other tumor types.
CONCLUSIONS: During pulmonary metastasectomy, adjusted diagnostic accuracy of ICG was 80.7%, and, importantly, 11.9% of metastasectomies contained viable tumors identified by ICG but not by preoperative imaging.

43062146.title: Return to School and Readmission Risk After Pain-Related Hospitalizations in Pediatric Sickle Cell Disease.
43062146.author: Connolly ME
43062146.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pain is the primary cause of inpatient admissions in sickle cell disease (SCD) and readmission is common. For school-aged youth, successful transition from the hospital necessitates school reentry. This study assessed rates of school return following a pain-related admission and the relationship between school return and readmission.
METHODS: Sixteen youth (7-17 years) admitted for SCD-related pain and caregivers completed daily surveys about school attendance and pain severity for 10 consecutive school days after discharge. Descriptive, independent samples t-test, and chi-square analyses were used to assess differences in pain, school attendance, and readmission.
RESULTS: On average, participants (age M = 13.75; 69% female; 75% HbSS) attended 6.13 out of 10 school days, with 25% returning the next school day after discharge and 13% attending all 10 days. Almost all (94%) reported ongoing pain throughout the monitoring period. Most youth (63%) exhibited variable school attendance after initial school return. Those with variable attendance attended fewer school days (M = 4.40, SD = 2.46) compared to "consistent school attenders" (M = 9, SD = 0.89), p < 0.001, and reported higher daily pain (MVariableAttenders = 3.78, SDVariableAttenders = 1.68; MConsistentAttenders = 1.47, SDConsistentAttenders = 0.81), p = 0.007. Half of "variable school attenders" were readmitted, compared to none of the consistent attenders, χ2 (df = 1) = 4.36, p = 0.037.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that school reentry after a pain-related hospitalization is difficult for many patients and essential to consider in discharge planning. Youth continue reporting pain following discharge, with some experiencing variable school attendance and readmission for pain. Promoting school attendance should be a core component of comprehensive SCD management plans, with implications for pain management and healthcare utilization.

43062145.title: Craniospinal Irradiation Dose De-Escalation With Chemotherapy in Pediatric Standard-Risk Medulloblastoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
43062145.author: Solis-Mata JS
43062145.abstract: Craniospinal irradiation (CSI) plus chemotherapy is standard for pediatric standard/average-risk medulloblastoma, but the safest de-escalated dose remains uncertain. We systematically reviewed four databases and meta-analyzed 5-year disease-control survival (DCS) and overall survival (OS). Fifteen studies were included. Modern 18/23.4-Gy CSI yielded 79.6% DCS and 85.3% OS. At 23.4 Gy, corresponding estimates were 81.0% and 86.7%; at 18 Gy, 71.3% and 79.1%. Current evidence supports 23.4 Gy as the most reproducible platform, whereas routine 18-Gy use is not supported outside prospectively selected, molecularly favorable populations.

43062118.title: Multimodality Care and Survival in Adolescents and Young Adults With Metastatic Non-Rhabdomyosarcoma Soft Tissue Sarcoma in California.
43062118.author: Alvarez E
43062118.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Approximately 20% of adolescents and young adults (AYA: ages 15-39) with non-rhabdomyosarcoma soft tissue sarcoma (NRSTS) are diagnosed with metastatic disease, which has a dismal prognosis. Optimal care is critical to improve outcomes, but there is no consensus on the best management approach. We sought to evaluate multimodality care (MMC) and survival among AYAs with metastatic NRSTS.
METHODS: We identified AYAs diagnosed during 2004-2022 with metastatic NRSTS in the California Cancer Registry. We defined MMC as first-line treatment receipt of surgery, chemotherapy, and radiation per the Children's Oncology Group ARST0332 protocol. We used multivariable logistic regression to evaluate associations of sociodemographic and clinical factors with receipt of MMC, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression to examine the impact of MMC on overall survival.
RESULTS: Of the 726 AYAs with metastatic NRSTS, 14% received MMC. A larger proportion of patients 15-25 years old who were treated by pediatric (vs. medical) oncologists received chemotherapy (96% vs. 75%), radiation (53% vs. 34%), and chemoradiation (51% vs. 25%). Older age (>21 years) was associated with decreased odds of receiving MMC. In patients ages 15-25, treatment by a pediatric (vs. medical) oncologist was associated with higher odds of receiving MMC (odds ratio [OR] = 3.4, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.33-8.72). Median overall survival was longer for patients receiving MMC (2.1 vs. 1.1 years), although associations did not remain statistically significant in the multivariable-adjusted model (HR = 0.89, CI = 0.68-1.16). Receiving all care at a specialized cancer center was associated with improved overall survival (HR = 0.63, CI = 0.49-0.81).
CONCLUSION: We found that only 14% of AYAs with metastatic NRSTS received MMC, which was impacted by age at diagnosis and physician specialty. Future research should investigate decision-making in patients with metastatic NRSTS and their providers, and its impact on outcomes.

43062073.author: Laditan M
43062073.abstract: Gene therapy in patients with severe sickle cell disease has been recently approved for commercial use, even in children. Clinical trials leading to approval were limited to patients with hemoglobin SS and Sβ0, due to the severity of disease in these patients. The efficacy of gene therapy in patients with hemoglobin SC disease is unknown. We provide details on treatment and clinical course of the first hemoglobin SC patient treated with gene therapy due to the severity of symptoms and the absence of any viable treatment options that could provide relief from the ravages of the disease.

43061901.title: A Phase IB Study to Evaluate the Safety and Feasibility of Nivolumab or Nivolumab With Azacitidine in Patients With Recurrent, Resectable Osteosarcoma: A Report From the National Pediatric Cancer Foundation.
43061901.author: Campbell ME
43061901.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Relapse rates following complete surgical resection (CSR) of pulmonary osteosarcoma recurrence remain high. We hypothesized that PD-1 inhibition with nivolumab (Nivo) combined with epigenetic priming using azacitidine (5-Aza) would be safe and augment systemic immune activation in patients with resectable pulmonary osteosarcoma relapse.
METHODS: This Phase I trial sought to establish the recommended Phase II dose (RP2D) of perioperative Nivo/5-Aza in patients ≤39 years old with isolated, resectable pulmonary osteosarcoma relapse. Three dose levels (DLs) were studied using a modified 3 + 3 design with dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) assessed from Day 1 of therapy to CSR. Patients received biweekly Nivo 3 mg/kg alone (DL1) or with 5-Aza at 60 or 75 mg/m2/day (DL2 and DL3) in 28-day cycles.
RESULTS: Twenty patients received therapy; 18 were evaluable for DLTs. DL3 exceeded the maximum tolerated dose (Grade 3 vomiting, prolonged Grade 4 neutropenia). Common adverse events included anemia, neutropenia, and nausea. Seventeen patients (85%) reached CSR after neoadjuvant therapy. Median event-free survival (EFS) was 3.3 months (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.7-7.7 months), and median overall survival was 21.1 months (95% CI: 10.1-42.6 months). Combination therapy was associated with evidence of systemic immune activation, including increases in IFN-γ, IL-1α, IL-1β, and CCL5.
CONCLUSION: The RP2D was Nivo 3 mg/kg and 5-Aza 60 mg/m2/day on Days 1-5 and 8-9. The combination was feasible and tolerable. EFS was limited in the context of a Phase I trial. These findings provide safety, feasibility, and exploratory immunologic data to inform future immunotherapy trials in osteosarcoma.

43061894.title: Timing of Eltrombopag Initiation and Treatment-Free Remission in Children With Persistent and Chronic Immune Thrombocytopenia: A Retrospective Tertiary-Center Cohort Study.
43061894.author: İzmir MA
43061894.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Eltrombopag is an established second-line therapy for children with persistent or chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP), but treatment-free remission after discontinuation and its relationship with treatment timing remain insufficiently defined. We evaluated eltrombopag outcomes, focusing on initiation timing and time to treatment-free remission.
PROCEDURE: This retrospective tertiary-center cohort included children with persistent or chronic ITP followed from December 2014 to December 2024. Of 81 patients, 41 received eltrombopag. Treatment-free remission was defined as maintaining a platelet count ≥50 × 109/L for at least six consecutive months without ITP-directed treatment and without bleeding or other clinical symptoms. Persistent- versus chronic-phase initiation was compared using Kaplan-Meier analysis and the log-rank test.
RESULTS: Overall, platelet response was achieved in 36/41 patients (88%), sustained platelet response in 23/41 (56%), and treatment-free remission in 14/41 (34%). In the 40-patient timing cohort, time to treatment-free remission was shorter with persistent-phase initiation than with chronic-phase initiation (log-rank p = 0.027); Kaplan-Meier estimated median times were 28 and 78 months, respectively. Among patients achieving treatment-free remission, a longer diagnosis-to-eltrombopag interval was associated with a longer eltrombopag-to-remission interval (rho = 0.543, p = 0.045, n = 14). Adverse events occurred in 8/41 patients (20%), with no permanent discontinuations.
CONCLUSIONS: Eltrombopag was associated with high platelet response rates and treatment-free remission in approximately one-third of treated children. Persistent-phase initiation was associated with shorter time to treatment-free remission than chronic-phase initiation. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to determine whether earlier eltrombopag initiation is associated with a higher likelihood of, or shorter time to, treatment-free remission.

43061850.title: Late Effects of (131)I-MIBG in Survivors of High-Risk Neuroblastoma: A Report From the Children's Oncology Group LEAHRN Study.
43061850.author: Kumar P
43061850.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Meta-iodobenzylguanidine radiolabeled with iodine-131 (131I-MIBG) is used to treat high-risk neuroblastoma (HRNBL). Late toxicities of 131I-MIBG have not been well studied due to limited survival of patients receiving this therapy for relapsed disease.
METHODS: The Children's Oncology Group LEAHRN study evaluated HRNBL survivors diagnosed after 2000 and alive at least 5 years from diagnosis. Clinical history and the prevalence of late effects were summarized for participants treated with 131I-MIBG (cases). Participants who did not receive 131I-MIBG were randomly selected and matched by age at diagnosis and relapse history (controls) in a 1:2 case-control study design. Chi-squared analysis was used to evaluate the association between 131I-MIBG and late toxicities.
RESULTS: Of 375 participants in the LEAHRN analytic cohort, 32 (8.5%) received 131I-MIBG. Differences in the proportion with thyroid toxicity and growth failure were observed but not statistically significant. The proportions of other major organ toxicities were not different between cases and controls, including subsequent malignancy.
DISCUSSION: No statistically significant differences were identified in the burden of late toxicities for HRNBL survivors treated with and without 131I-MIBG. A small sample size likely limited the ability to detect statistically significant differences. Our data provide information for follow-up care of 131I-MIBG-treated survivors and clinical trial design.

43049263.title: Total Serum IgG Is a Poor Surrogate for Pneumococcal Protection Following Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation in Pediatric Sickle Cell Disease.
43049263.author: Needum A
43049263.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children with sickle cell disease (SCD) have functional asplenia and a higher risk of invasive pneumococcal disease. While allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is curative, post-transplant immune reconstitution is heterogeneous. Total serum immunoglobulin G (IgG) is widely used to gauge humoral recovery yet may not reflect pneumococcal serotype-specific seroprotection.
METHODS: We performed a single-center retrospective cohort study of pediatric patients with SCD who underwent myeloablative matched sibling donor HSCT at Texas Children's Hospital between 2005 and 2024 and obtained pneumococcal serotype-specific antibody titers at approximately 1 year. Seroprotection was defined as an antibody concentration ≥1.3 µg/mL in ≥70% of 14 tested serotypes. Longitudinal total IgG, IgA, IgM, tetanus titers, and lymphocyte subsets (CD3+, CD4+, CD8+, CD19+) were analyzed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and penalized multivariable logistic regression were performed (n = 51).
RESULTS: Of 51 patients, 32 (62.7%) achieved pneumococcal serotype-specific protection at approximately 1 year. Total IgG correlated weakly with protection at all time points (r = 0.28-0.38). Day +365 total IgG did not differ between protected and unprotected patients (p = 0.134); at commonly used thresholds between 400 and 600 mg/dL, sensitivity was 97%, but specificity was 0%, and all unprotected patients exceeded 600 mg/dL. Day +365 IgG showed limited discrimination (AUC 0.63). Broad quantitative lymphocyte subsets were also not significantly correlated with the proportion of protective pneumococcal serotypes. No invasive pneumococcal disease occurred during follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: Normal total serum IgG does not reliably identify pneumococcal serotype-specific seroprotection after HSCT in pediatric SCD. Serotype-specific antibody assessment provides information not captured by total IgG alone.

43049245.title: Recommended Phase 2 Dose for Abemaciclib in Combination With Temozolomide in Pediatric and Young Adult Patients With Relapsed/Refractory Solid Tumors: Results From Study JPCS Part B.
43049245.author: Lassaletta A
43049245.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) pathway aberrations, including CDK4 or CCND1 amplification, CDKN2A/B loss, retinoblastoma (RB) dysregulation, and cyclin D overexpression, are relevant for pediatric cancers. Abemaciclib, a selective CDK4/6 inhibitor with preferential CDK4 activity and central nervous system (CNS) penetration, induces sustained G1 arrest. Preclinical pediatric models show additive or synergistic activity with temozolomide, supporting further evaluation. Here, the recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D) for abemaciclib with temozolomide is defined in children and young adults with relapsed/refractory solid tumors.
PROCEDURE: JPCS Part B was an open-label, multicenter Phase 1b study using a 3 + 3 design to evaluate continuous abemaciclib (70-115 mg/m2 orally BID) with temozolomide (100-150 mg/m2 orally days 1-5) in 21-day cycles. The primary objective was RP2D determination based on dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) and pharmacokinetics. Secondary objectives included safety and antitumor activity.
RESULTS: Twenty-six patients (median age 11 years; range, 1-18) with heavily pretreated relapsed/refractory tumors were enrolled. The RP2D was established as 115 mg/m2 abemaciclib BID on Days 1-21, with 150 mg/m2 temozolomide on Days 1-5 of 21-day cycles, based on two DLTs (thrombocytopenia), one at the RP2D. The maximum tolerated dose was not reached. Toxicities reflected expected myelosuppression and predominantly low-grade gastrointestinal events. Together, 35% and 19% of patients experienced Grades 3 and 4 treatment-related toxicities, respectively. Steady-state abemaciclib concentrations aligned with adult efficacy-associated ranges, with no drug-drug interactions. Three patients (12%) achieved partial responses and 10 (38%) stable disease, yielding 50% disease control. Three patients had sustained disease control with >6 months on treatment.
CONCLUSIONS: Abemaciclib plus temozolomide is feasible and well-tolerated and shows preliminary antitumor activity, supporting further evaluation in Phase 2 trials.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT04238819.

43046656.title: Immune Trait Polygenic Scores Among Survivors of Hodgkin Lymphoma.
43046656.author: Tark JY
43046656.abstract: Epidemiologic evidence links immune-related conditions to Hodgkin lymphoma (HL), but the shared genetic architecture remains unclear. Using data from the St. Jude Survivorship Portal, pre-computed polygenic risk scores (PRSs) for 12 allergy and immune-related traits were compared between 794 survivors of HL and 3664 survivors of non-hematologic malignancies using logistic regression to estimate adjusted odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Higher eczema/dermatitis PRS was associated with increased odds of HL relative to non-hematologic malignancies (OR = 1.14, 95% CI 1.05-1.25). These exploratory findings suggest some immune-related genetic variation may be enriched in survivors of HL.

43042859.title: Trametinib in Neurofibromatosis Type 1-Associated Plexiform Neurofibroma-Real-World Data From the SACHA-France Study.
43042859.author: Vanderkelen CR
43042859.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF-1) frequently leads to inoperable, symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas (PNs) with limited therapeutic options. This study evaluates the real-world activity and safety of the MEK inhibitor trametinib in pediatric NF-1 patients with inoperable PNs in France.
METHODS: We analyzed pediatric patients enrolled in the SACHA-France study (NCT04477681) who received trametinib for inoperable PNs between 01/2020 and 01/2026. Antitumor activity was evaluated by treating physicians using response evaluation criteria in solid tumors (RECIST) 1.1 criteria. Adverse events (AEs) were graded per Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) v5.0. Clinical benefit data were collected retrospectively.
RESULTS: Twenty-three patients (median age: 6 years [range: 0-17]) were included. Clinical benefit occurred in 87% (20/23), mainly through pain reduction (86% of symptomatic patients, 12/14). RECIST assessment showed partial response in 4% (1/23), stable disease in 87% (20/23), and progression in 9% (2/23). AEs occurred in 96% of patients, predominantly cutaneous (96%) and Grade 1-2. Four Grade 3 AEs were reported (osteitis, paronychia [n = 2], elevated creatine kinase), prompting discontinuation in 2 cases. Median treatment duration was 33 months [range: 1-58]. Treatment was discontinued in seven patients for prolonged stable disease, four for disease progression (two clinical, two radiological), two for severe AEs, and one for poor adherence. Nine patients remained on treatment at cutoff.
CONCLUSION: Trametinib provided notable clinical benefit and disease stabilization in pediatric NF-1-associated PNs, despite limited RECIST-defined tumor shrinkage. The safety profile was manageable and consistent with known data. Comparative studies with other MEK inhibitors are warranted to optimize treatment strategies.

43042802.title: Caregiver Primary Language and Barriers to Care at Diagnosis of Pediatric Acute Leukemia.
43042802.author: Gonzalez Hinojosa MD
43042802.abstract: Timely diagnosis is critical in pediatric acute leukemia. This study evaluated the relationship between caregiver primary language, access to care, and disease acuity among 62 children with acute myeloid leukemia or acute lymphoblastic leukemia treated at two children's hospitals. The languages evaluated were primarily English and Spanish. The validated Barriers to Care Questionnaire measured access to care across five domains: pragmatics, skills, expectations, marginalization, and knowledge-and-beliefs. Leukemia disease acuity was assessed using laboratory markers. Caregivers with a primary language other than English reported greater skills-related barriers and their children presented more frequently with hyperuricemia, potentially indicating higher leukemia burden and acuity. These findings highlight language-related navigation barriers as potential contributors to healthcare access.

43042581.title: Preserved Right Ventricular Function With Early Remodeling in Pediatric Sickle Cell Disease: Comprehensive Echocardiographic Assessment and Longitudinal Analysis.
43042581.author: Tannoury T
43042581.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiopulmonary complications contribute substantially to morbidity in sickle cell disease (SCD), but right ventricular (RV) involvement in children remains incompletely characterized. We aimed to assess RV structure and function in pediatric SCD using conventional echocardiography and two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography, and to examine associations with clinical features, hydroxyurea use, hemolysis markers, and longitudinal changes.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of children with SCD followed at a single tertiary center from 2015 to 2023. Clinical, laboratory, and treatment data were collected, and age- and sex-matched healthy children served as controls. Echocardiographic assessment included RV dimensions, systolic indices, tricuspid regurgitant velocity (TRv), and RV free-wall strain.
RESULTS: A total of 185 children were included (118 with SCD and 67 controls; mean age, 11.7 ± 5.3 years). Compared with controls, children with SCD had larger RV dimensions, slightly lower RV fractional area change, and higher TRv, whereas RV free-wall strain remained largely preserved. RV strain correlated with age, RV size, fractional area change, and TRv, but not with hydroxyurea use, anemia, hemolysis markers, or most clinical complications. RV indices were similar across genotypes. Elevated TRv (≥2.5 m/s) was present in 12.9% of patients. Longitudinal follow-up demonstrated stable RV function over time.
CONCLUSIONS: Children with SCD exhibit subtle RV remodeling and mildly increased pulmonary pressure despite preserved RV systolic function. These findings suggest that early right-heart changes in pediatric SCD are predominantly structural and hemodynamic rather than functional.

43050622.title: Impact of Social Isolation and Psychological Distress on Overall Survival in Cancer: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
43050622.author: Zeng D
43050622.abstract:
PURPOSE: Social isolation is associated with increased mortality in cancer, but prior studies often examined single cancer types, approximated social isolation using composite indices, and rarely accounted for co-occurring psychological distress. We evaluated the independent associations of five social isolation domains and psychological distress with overall survival (OS) in a large population-based cancer cohort.
METHODS: We included 45,651 patients who completed the Psychosocial Screen for Cancer-Revised (PSSCAN-R) at their initial BC Cancer visit between April 18, 2011, and December 30, 2016. Five social isolation domains, depression symptoms, and anxiety symptoms were derived from the PSSCAN-R. OS was estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods, and independent associations were evaluated using multivariable Cox regression adjusting for age, sex, and metastatic status.
RESULTS: Among the cohort (mean age 64.9 years, 55.2% female), 32.5% screened positive for at least 1 social isolation domain, most commonly living alone (23.0%) or recent partner loss (10.9%). In unadjusted analyses, all five isolation domains, depression, and anxiety were associated with reduced OS (all P < .05). A composite social isolation score showed a graded, dose-response association, with the hazard of death increasing approximately 9% per additional domain. In adjusted models, lack of regular social contact (hazard ratio [HR], 1.29 [95% CI, 1.17 to 1.41]), living alone (HR, 1.18 [95% CI, 1.13 to 1.22]), depression (HR, 1.43 [95% CI, 1.37 to 1.48]), and anxiety (HR, 1.23 [95% CI, 1.19 to 1.28]) were each independently associated with mortality.
CONCLUSION: Specific, individually screenable domains of social isolation and psychological distress were independently associated with mortality in cancer. Because these domains can be captured with brief self-report items within psychosocial screening, which is increasingly standard in oncology, social isolation screening represents a low-burden addition to risk stratification and supportive care prioritization.

43045665.title: Estimates of breast cancer screening benefit in older women to inform patient-centered care.
43045665.author: Schoenborn NL
43045665.abstract:
PURPOSE: When to stop breast cancer screening remains uncertain. The USPSTF recommends screening to age 74. Modeling estimates on screening benefit after age 74 are 5-12 average life-years gained (LYG) per 1000 women, which may be a useful benchmark for considering stopping screening. Existing LYG estimates do not incorporate individualized cancer risk or individualized life expectancy and involve numerous assumptions in simulation models. We aimed to estimate screening benefit in older women that incorporate frailty/comorbidity and breast cancer risk.
METHODS: Using SEER-Medicare data (1999-2017), we constructed cohorts to estimate screening benefit at age 70 and 75, respectively. We included women continuously enrolled in fee-for-service Medicare for ≥5 years and were breast cancer free before the age of interest. We obtained screening-associated breast cancer mortality risk reductions from a previous emulated trial. We combined these with individualized breast cancer mortality risk and individualized competing mortality risk to calculate average LYG from continuing annual screening over 8 years. Estimates were stratified by race and comorbidity/frailty.
RESULTS: Average LYG from screening ranged from 4.7-20.5 life-years per 1000 women in the age 70 cohort (n = 204,288), 3.4-13.6 life-years per 1000 women in the age 75 cohort (n = 193,398). Those with higher comorbidities/frailty had lower average LYG. Those with Hispanic/Asian/other race had the lowest LYG whereas Black women had the highest LYG.
CONCLUSION: Average LYGs from breast cancer screening based on population level data are small in older women, with important variations by health status and race, which should be considered in clinical discussions and screening recommendations.

43064682.title: Cancer symptom severity progression among adults with severe psychiatric illness: a matched cohort study.
43064682.author: Yu X
43064682.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Structural-, system-, and individual-level barriers may create difficulty in symptom management for adults diagnosed with cancer living with severe psychiatric illness (SPI). We investigated differences in the overall trajectories of long-term symptom progression between patients with and without an inpatient SPI history.
METHODS: This population-based matched cohort study used health administrative data of Ontario adults diagnosed with cancer between 2007 and 2021. Adults with SPI were matched 1:5 to those without mental illness. We applied Markov multistate models to analyze pain, nausea, and wellbeing transitions over five years between symptom severity states (none, mild, moderate, severe, death). We estimated transition rate ratios (RR) and 60-day transition probabilities to evaluate symptom trajectory differences.
RESULTS: Among 6,235 patients with SPI and 31,175 matches, patients with SPI exhibited significantly accelerated symptom deterioration. For pain, SPI patients had elevated rates of 'none-to-mild' (RR = 1.69, 95% CI: 1.58-1.82) and 'mild-to-moderate' transitions (RR = 2.02, 95% CI: 1.83-2.22) compared to patients without SPI. They also demonstrated elevated rates of death from a pain-free state (RR = 3.05, 95% CI: 2.85-3.25), possibly reflecting unrecorded symptom decline and different mortality risks. Conversely, SPI patients demonstrated lower transition probabilities of pain improvement; at 60 days, patients with moderate pain were 8.4% less likely to improve to mild pain (SPI: 27.8%, 95% CI: 0.0%-28.5%; non-SPI: 36.2%, 95% CI: 35.8%-36.5%). Nausea and wellbeing exhibited similar trends.
CONCLUSION: These findings of differences in cancer symptom progression between individuals with and without an inpatient SPI history highlight the need for tailored interventions for this vulnerable population.

43062195.title: Health-related social needs, biological aging, and long-term mortality risk among a nationally representative cohort of cancer survivors.
43062195.author: Han X
43062195.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Unmet health-related social needs (HRSNs, such as food insecurity, and inadequate health insurance coverage) may interplay with accelerated biological aging, and lead to higher mortality risks. We examined the associations of HRSNs with long-term mortality risks along with accelerated aging in a nationally representative cohort of cancer survivors.
METHODS: Cancer survivors aged 20-84 years were identified from the 1999-2010 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) with linked mortality follow-up through December 31, 2022. Data on HRSNs, including poverty, lack of home ownership, food insecurity, unemployment, lack of health insurance, and coverage instability, were collected at in-person interviews. Biological aging was measured by a validated composite of biomarkers. Associations of HRSNs with all-cause and cancer-specific mortality risks were examined using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models, and associations of HRSNs with accelerated biological aging were examined using multivariable linear regression models.
RESULTS: Among 715 cancer survivors (mean age 59.8 at interview, 64.3% women), 261 (36.3%) had any HRSNs and 21 (2.2%) had ≥3 HRSNs. In ≥ 12 years of follow-up, there were 315 deaths, including 103 from cancer. Having ≥3 HRSNs (compared to 0) was associated with an increased risk of death (Hazard Ratio=3.12, 95%CI=1.57-6.21) and 0.46 (95%CI=0.07-0.85) years of accelerated aging. Individual HRSNs were also associated with higher mortality risks and accelerated aging.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that proactively addressing HRSNs leveraging the biosocial framework may improve well-being and health outcomes among cancer survivors. Investing in public assistance programs and policy efforts may benefit individuals across the healthcare continuum.

43056125.title: Chest Computed Tomography Receipt Beyond 5 Years After Lung Cancer Diagnosis and Survival.
43056125.author: Yoon DW
43056125.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Long-term lung cancer (LC) survivors remain at risk of LC events (LCEs), including late recurrence and second primary LC, beyond 5 years after diagnosis, but the role of computed tomography (CT) surveillance beyond 5 years remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether CT receipt beyond 5 years after LC diagnosis is associated with LCEs and survival.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This nationwide population-based cohort study used sequential target trial emulation with monthly eligibility reassessment and time-updated propensity score matching based on data from the Korean National Health Insurance Service database. Patients diagnosed with LC from 2006 to 2019 were followed up through December 31, 2024. Long-term LC survivors were eligible for trial entry 5.5 years after diagnosis if they had no administrative evidence of active or recurrent LC, a prior LCE, or another primary cancer. Data were analyzed between January 1, 2026, and February 28, 2026.
EXPOSURES: CT receipt beyond 5 years after LC diagnosis, defined as chest CT during the 1-month assessment window at each monthly trial baseline, compared with no CT receipt.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was LCE occurrence, defined by new LC-specific special copayment registration after the monthly trial baseline. Secondary outcomes were all-cause mortality, surgical resection after LCE detection, and subsequent mortality.
RESULTS: The cohort of 55 694 LC survivors (mean [SD] age, 63.3 [10.9] years; 58.0% male) contributed 2 629 462 eligible person-trials. Matching yielded 583 756 person-trials per group. During a median (IQR) follow-up of 2.74 (1.16-5.18) years, CT receipt was associated with a higher incidence of LCEs (2.49% vs 1.97% per year; hazard ratio [HR], 1.28 [95% CI, 1.26-1.29]) and lower all-cause mortality rate (2.62% vs 4.33% per year; HR, 0.66 [95% CI, 0.65-0.67]) compared with no CT receipt. Among patients with an LCE, CT receipt was associated with greater odds of surgical resection after LCE (odds ratio, 1.46 [95% CI, 1.41-1.52]) and a lower subsequent mortality risk (HR, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.61-0.64]). These associations were observed more frequently among females (HR, 0.47 [95% CI, 0.44-0.49]), older adults (HR, 0.57 [95% CI, 0.54-0.60]), and never smokers (HR, 0.55 [95% CI, 0.53-0.57]).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study, CT receipt beyond 5 years after LC diagnosis was associated with increased detection of LCEs, greater use of surgical resection after an LCE, and a lower all-cause mortality rate. These findings support further evaluation of risk-adapted CT surveillance beyond 5 years in selected LC survivors.

43044154.title: Effectiveness of remote symptom monitoring with clinical feedback in patients with breast cancer under active treatment: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
43044154.author: de Almeida ABB
43044154.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Remote symptom monitoring may improve health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in breast cancer, but the role of clinical feedback is unclear. We evaluated remote symptom monitoring with clinical feedback (RSM-CF) during active treatment.
METHODS: This PROSPERO-registered (CRD420261359848) systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA 2020. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CENTRAL to February 28, 2026 (updated June 20, 2026) for randomized controlled trials of digital symptom monitoring with clinical feedback in adults with breast cancer under active treatment. The primary outcome was post-intervention HRQoL. We used RoB 2, random-effects meta-analyses, and trial sequential analysis (TSA).
FINDINGS: Eleven trials (1424 patients) were included. RSM-CF was associated with a small, non-significant improvement in HRQoL (standardized mean difference [SMD] 0·23, 95% CI -0·03-0·50; I² = 70·4%) and total QoL scores (SMD 0·28, 95% CI -0·02-0·59). Symptom burden (SMD -0·64, 95% CI -1·66-0·38), self-efficacy (SMD 0·02, 95% CI -0·18-0·23), and treatment adherence (risk ratio 1·09, 95% CI 0·96-1·23) did not differ significantly. Three trials had low risk of bias; eight had some concerns. In TSA, the required information size was not reached; TSA was not feasible for symptom burden. Certainty of evidence was low for most outcomes.
INTERPRETATION: Current evidence does not establish a consistent benefit of RSM-CF on HRQoL, symptom burden, self-efficacy, or treatment adherence during active breast cancer treatment. Point estimates favoured RSM-CF for HRQoL and symptom burden, but heterogeneity and insufficient information limit certainty.
FUNDING: None.

43067546.title: Minimally genotoxic conditioning increases donor chimerism in a mismatched murine transplant model for sickle cell disease.
43067546.author: Ali MAE
43067546.abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) causes severe complications, organ damage, and premature death, with hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) being the only curative option. Myeloablative conditioning (MAC) is used for traditional allogeneic HCT and autologous gene therapies, but it is often too toxic for adults with organ damage. Non-myeloablative (NMA) haploidentical HCT can expand the donor pool and be applied to patients with organ impairment. Still, two major concerns face NMA haploidentical HCT: graft failure and recipient-derived hematologic malignancies. Therefore, our aim has shifted towards maximizing donor chimerism levels. This work explores non-genotoxic antibody-based conditioning in a mismatched murine HCT model for SCD. We targeted two cell-surface receptors: CD45, a pan-hematopoietic cell marker, and CD117, a receptor expressed mainly on hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells. Saporin (sap), the drug payload, is released intracellularly, halting protein synthesis and inducing cell death. Our base conditioning regimen also included post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PT-Cy) and sirolimus. We utilized an allogeneic murine HCT model in which female donor Balb/c bone marrow (BM) cells were transplanted into female C57Bl/6J recipients. Peripheral blood (PB) analysis showed that conjugated antibodies successfully induced mixed chimerism, whereas the naked version failed. Long-term follow-up (24 weeks) showed that only CD45-sap exhibited an upward trajectory of PB total, B cell, and T cell chimerism, and stable myeloid chimerism. In contrast, all other groups showed diminishing levels of chimerism. Next, we adapted an additional lymphocyte-depleting approach using anti-mouse Thy1.2 antibody (Thy1.2). Unlike CD45-sap, PB analysis showed synergy between CD117-sap and thy1.2, resulting in significantly higher chimerism levels than in mice receiving CD117-sap combined with 50 cGy TBI. Additionally, mice that received the combined CD117-sap and thy1.2 regimen experienced early fatal anemia, but this could be reversed by a single blood transfusion. HbSS Townes mice are an established model of SCD, with a baseline hemolytic anemia. Consequently, three blood transfusions were administered the week before conditioning. Mice were conditioned with 200 cGy TBI or CD117-sap, along with Thy1.2. Hb levels showed a severe drop on day 2 pre-HCT and day 6 post-HCT, followed by restoration to normal levels by day 13 post-HCT in both groups. Chimerism analysis at 24 weeks post-HCT showed that Townes mice conditioned with CD117-sap had significantly higher chimerism levels than mice that received 200 cGy TBI. Further, Hb levels were significantly higher in CD117-sap-conditioned mice. HPLC analysis at 24 weeks post-HCT showed that recipients conditioned with CD117-sap exhibited donor-derived Hb. Furthermore, BM analysis at 24 weeks post-HCT showed a significant increase in the frequencies of donor-derived short- and long-term hematopoietic stem cells in CD117-sap-conditioned recipients, further confirming successful long-term engraftment. Finally, we show that long-term blood transfusions improve survival, allowing us to study this HCT approach in the previously fragile Townes HbSS mice. In summary, CD117-sap, in combination with thy1.2, PT-Cy, and sirolimus, is a promising novel NMA conditioning regimen that achieves high levels of donor chimerism in the Townes SCD mouse model and can reverse SCD.
